analysis.name: Amber Peters
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: To be honest her class is pretty easy. There are in class questions you must answer for attendance/grade, but class material is pretty easy. Exams are half multiple choice half written but again not hard. She is gone doing research a lot so will have canceled classes/ TA ran classes which is nice. My downfall was not paying attention in class

Dr. Peters is super nice! She taught half of the lectures, and Dr. Peacor taught the other half. I think that she had simpler topics, so it was easier to understand her. The rest of the class was quite difficult outside of her lectures. Something that made things a bit difficult was her lack of study materials for exams.

Dr. Peters is a great professor! She obviously knows what she's talking about and welcomes any questions or comments on the material. She makes an effort to get to know the class and lectures are engaging and interesting. Attendance is not required but participation matters! Exams are written response but easy if you go to class and participate.

I loved Dr. Peters! I enjoyed taking her Great Lakes Bio class. It wasn't a ton of work and the quizzes felt fair. This semester, she offered that if you had over a 90% in the class you didn't have to take the final exam so make sure you attend class! There were no attendance drops but a few chances for extra credit.

Dr. Peters is a good professor and she is obviously very knowledgeable in her field. However, her grading is weird sometimes and her quizzes/tests are all short answer. I would take her class again, but be prepared for it to be slightly unorganized and for her to be gone several lectures.

analysis.name: Ashley Moore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Moore, and I had her for TE101. After reading negative reviews, it seems that people are upset due to the difficult discussions that were had in class, but Dr. Moore was always respectful to everyone while sharing her thoughts, and I never felt attacked or judged. She can be quite opinionated, but once you're used to it, it's all good.

I liked Ashley! She was super sweet and cared about our personal lives, would ask a group question at the start of every class. Class is only 50 min but flew by. Last 6ish weeks are student led presentations. Didn't ever really want to skip this class. Easy homework and the papers aren't bad at all. Would take class with her again any time!
Professor Ashley is caring, fun and genuine. I loved her class and woukd definitely take one of her classes again. She is very understanding and down to earth. Beautiful soul.
Removed a student from her class for difference of opinions, the TE 101 and 102 classes are a complete joke and waste of time and content.
Had us turn in a rough draft, and then graded it on accuracy. 0/10, wouldn't recommend, would choose a different teacher.

analysis.name: Alexandria Davis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Alexandria is an awesome dance professor! She cares so much for her students and makes class like a fun workout! Totally recommend! I will keep taking her classes!

Alexandra is a kind person who is very passionate. But from a dancer perspective I feel I didn't learn much from what I thought the class was going to be. Along with that many things we did in class and talked about made me uncomfortable. If you are a dancer and wanting to dance I don't recommend

I love Alexandria! I am not a dancer by nature but I had a great time in her class. She really cares about your progress and is super understanding. I think I've really improved because of her. I would highly recommend her class

analysis.name: Amy Pollock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 205 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor & very clear for those who may not understand chemistry well. Free book is a bonus. Very easy class. Participation and attendance required. Homework and recitation are "A for effort" grades. Short lectures. Fair amount of homework, but always short and easy. Easy tests if you study. If you did well in high school chem, you're fine

Amy is amazing. She is a super kind and a cute lady. However, if you do not come to the lectures, you will fail. Class material is basic chem and Amy teaches it super well. She is very passionate and explains every thing in great detail. There are about 2 easy homeworks a week.  Overall, if you come to class and pay attention, you should pass.

Dr. Pollock is a great professor and one of the best I've had at MSU. If you actually pay attention to the lectures then you will be fine. She makes chemistry easy to understand and a 4.0 is not very hard to get.

She is hands down one of the best professors that I ever had. The lectures were very easy to follow, but to understand the posted slides, you most often had to attend lecture. The exams tested your knowledge, but if you go and get outside help the exams are a piece of cake - and you can get extra credit. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

You need to attend lecture to understand anything, and then outside of lecture you need to look at the slides and make sure you understand what is going on. Study... a lot. The exams are nothing like what's done in lecture or recitation so make sure you look at the practice exams before hand and make sure you know how to do everything on them.

analysis.name: Patrick Arnold
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Arnold is one of the most caring professors you will have at msu. They are very understanding and want you to succeed. There is an assignment due every other week that only takes about 30 minutes or less to do and 2 campus event reflections. As long as you complete your work the best you can, they will give you a 100!

Super nice and actually cares for students. The class itself is super easy and has discussion questions every other week which is really nice. Grading is super lenient and the assignments and readings are easy. Sometimes you do not even half to read the book to answer the discussion questions. Honors option is also easy.

i took this as an elective, easiest class ever. prof arnold is very sweet and such a nice person. this class requires little to no work. there's 1 online assignment a week that normally took ab 10-20 mins. u have to go to 2 events of ur choice during the semester. no tests/final. love prof arnold!!!

Professor Arnold is a great teacher and you can tell they genuinely care about their students. It's really easy to get a 4.0 as long as you complete the assignments. Probably the easiest class I've ever taken and doing the assignment each week didn't take much time.

Professor Arnolds class was amazing. I felt that the material was good and easy to understand, and they were extremely understanding for every single assignment that there was. There were also no exams! Overall I really liked this class.

analysis.name: Amanda Flaim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: felt incredibly babied and micromanaged. Specifically, rubrics had word counts for specific paragraphs, and she would walk around the lecture to make sure you were paying attention and didn't have your laptop out were some things that really pissed me off. She brought valuable information to class but I felt  like I was in 6th grade

I loved having Professor Flaim as my professor for MC 201. She can be a difficult grader and rarely gives "perfect" scores, but she will help you improve your work if you're struggling. Note: Her office hours can be busy. She's passionate about the topics she teaches, make sure to participate in class!!

Flaim is nice, and passionate. She cares for her students and her cause. However, she frequently goes off topic, which stops you from getting answers to your questions. She also grades harder than the other professors so you will probably have to work harder than your fellow classmates.
She is very understanding towards students and is passionate about her teaching.

Tough grader, all readings are similar and not interesting. The class is tailored for specific people. It is unorganized and good luck getting a 4.0 on a paper. Her grading makes absolutely no sense. Would not wish this on my worst enemy

analysis.name: Sue Allen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 190 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Poor teaching style. Talks too much before class then rushes at the end, overall not organized in the slightest (which I need in a professor) her explanations are not cohesive/helpful. Treated class like high school, she's very funny but not a good math professor fit, she should be a highschool history teacher! If you're bad at math don't take her.

I didn't enjoy professor Allen's teaching style. She treated the class like a highschool class, and showed us the same sort of respect as highschoolers. She tends to start talking way before class started and usually ended class late. She was also sensitive about people leaving early. She was fine, but I didn't love her teaching style or anything.

She's a great teacher. I am terrible at math but I still managed a 3.0. I suggest attending all lectures and taking notes. Do webwork the same day as the lecture so it is easier. If you struggle GO TO OFFICE HOURS or MLC! She will help you with your homework and with your grades. She gives practice problems that aren't due, but really help.

such a difficult professor, so much to do on webwork but she says its not important. You only learn in lecture (not recitation), so if you miss the lecture or part of the lecture you're done for. She won't answer questions that she answered in class already, which made it feel like you couldn't email her with questions, also won't reteach concepts.

If you're good at math do other students a favor and take her lecture (people not good at math will struggle with her teaching style so let them take a better prof.) Lectures are too short for the amount of chatting she does. I retaught myself content after class. She's sweet and wants to help you when 1-on-1 but she should teach a smaller class.

analysis.name: Alan Arbogast
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: ISS205 is mainly a prerequisite, and the median grade across every professor for this course is a 4. However, he attempts to be different and unique by making this class harder than every other ISS. He believes a small percentage deserves a 4 even if everyone does well. This makes it completely unfair for his students compared to other professors

Really like the guy and his lectures, but I feel like he should make the lecture material actually available to the students instead of penalizing them for not retaining every word of what he says. His slides are basically just pictures, and are hard to make sense of after the class. His exams were fairly tough, but easy enough to get atleast an 80

Professor Alan is an all-around good guy, and I genuinely enjoyed waking up and going to his class. While the tests can be challenging sometimes, if you do the proper studying beforehand, then you should be well prepared. Always in a good mood and made learning interesting, relevant, and fun. Would highly recommend him to anyone.

There are 3 tests throughout the course which are the only assignments in the class. The class is super lecture heavy, but the professor goes off on tangents that aren't relevant a lot so it's important you pay attention because his slides also don't give you a lot of information. He's a great person though and super nice and do the class readings!

Very very hard course for an ISS 200 level. He's an interactive and nice Prof. I would save yourself the trouble and take a different course. Way too hard to be a 200 level. You have zero assignments, class is based off 3 exams (including the final.) The exams can be tricky and require lots of studying. You must attend every class! No curve either!

analysis.name: Amanda Lorenz-Reaves
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I could say the class is easy, or I could say that the material was explained so well and so well understood that the class seemed easy. Isn't that the goal as a good teacher to ensure students are learning all the material? Mission accomplished.

Clearly passionate about her lectures and it shows, they were all super easy to follow and interesting. The 2 Homework assignments are fun and don't take much time. In class participation assignments create interesting discussions, and students go to the MSU bug house at the end of the semester!

LOVEDDD Dr. Lorenz! She is very sweet and funny. This is an online class held over zoom so you'll have daily in class participation and pre-class readings, 3 home work, and 4 exams (all of which are open note). Genuinely enjoyed this class as her lectures are interesting and you can tell she is passionate about her work. Could not recommend enough!

I adored Professor Lorenz! She was incredibly gracious with RCPD extensions, and provided stress-free assignments. Every quiz and test was open resource, with plenty of time to complete the task. Lectures were engaging and interesting. She felicitated a calming learning environment while also sharing her passions. I cannot recommend enough!

Easiest ISB 201 class if you are willing to show up to class. She does in class papers for attendance (so easy you barely have to pay attention) basically your entire grade is attendance, a few 1 page papers & exams. The exams are very very easy. Super kind prof! Highly recommend her but dont get stuck in the 8:30am you wont make it.

analysis.name: Barb Gerber
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She is so nice and always cares for her students. She is very accessible outside of class and responds to emails very fast. She uses a sheet of paper to mark attendance and it does not matter if you are a couple minutes late to class. Would take her again and am convinced that she is the best teacher of this subject. Grade-100%
She is the best professor I had my freshman year. She is very caring and wants to see her students succeed. She is very flexible with grades.

Barb was a great professor. She really understands her students and the amount of work we have to do. We had deadlines on papers but she always moved them to about a week later. She took out a whole assignment because she thought we didnt have time. Definitely take her hybrid class, there was minimal work. And the papers were not even that long.

If you can, take the hybrid class because I do not see the point of going to a two hour writing class twice a week with the work that she assigns to us. Everything is very straight forward and most of her unit schedules are clear. I disliked how our assignments kept getting pushed back and things were graded late. She rarely responds to emails.

Barb SHOULD BE THE ONLY WRA PROFESSOR YOU TAKE! One time I forgot to turn in my paper by almost 3 weeks and she let it slide and gave me a full grade on it! Very nice and understanding, easy grader, easy assignments, easy 4.0, do not miss on the best opportunity to have the best WRA Professor in the world

analysis.name: Bethany Furqueron
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. Uses in-class activities and explains concepts simply, making the content really program into your brain. Homework is consistent and actually helps a lot with studying. If you go to help room she's really personable and very nice to talk to.

This was Dr. Furqueron's first time teaching this class, it didn't seem like it at all. She is so knowledgeable of the material and made sure everyone had a clear understanding of the content for the exams. Her lectures were engaging with group work. She is just a caring, encouraging person. Definitely one of the best professors I've had so far.

She makes the lectures super interesting, which cannot be said about most professors. She cares if you understand the material and is super helpful when it comes to questions. It is very easy to get points off on all of the assignments in here but overall she is an amazing professor.
Super amazing class would take agian.
Dr. Furqueron is quite actually the best instructor I have ever had! Her class is set up in a way where you really learn the material and it's enjoyable to go to class!!!!!!

analysis.name: Jan Brascamp
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very chill professor, more than half way through the semester and we havent had a full length class yet. Answers questions through out lecture and his powerpoints are very well structured. You can tell he really cares about his students & is willing to help!

Brascamp is a very nice prof, and his class is pretty interesting. This class does have A LOT of content, so the exams can be a bit hard, but if you study, you will do fine. 60% of the lectures are mandatory for attending and there are studies you have to do, but they are easy. Exams are massive part of grade, so beware of that

This is one of the easiest psych classes I have ever taken. The professor doesn't go in-depth, which is nice since it keeps the exams really straightforward. It is test-heavy, but honestly, the questions are super easy if you actually study and understand the material. He uses PowerPoints, SO if you miss class, you can just read the slides.

I would recommend. Yes this class is hard and yes it is mainly lecture + exam-based. Brascamp's slides are amazing though, he is the first psych prof I've had that I genuinely learned from. He is passionate, gives tons of visuals, and explains very everything well. For exams, if you just study the slides and make a quizlet, u will be just fine.

His lectures are very heavy in content and he moves decently fast through the slides. He doesn't do much extra talking outside of what is written on the slide. Attendance isn't mandatory but you do get extra credit for going to class. There are no quizzes, just experiments and SONA. You'll definitely need to prepare for exams, but they're not bad.

analysis.name: Bryan Ellis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Super time-consuming projects that are impossible to get 100%.
He uses iClicker + geo so get ready formind-numbing lectures, participation is 10%
Projects requiring teamwork CANNOT BE DONE ALONE so socialize or die (15%grade).
For the final, goodluck learning how to use OMEKA(super confusing)
If you took this class because you were late. Good Luck.

The class isn't that difficult but the professor is SO BORING. His lectures are mandatory, pointless, and so so slow, and he always takes random pauses when he talks that makes you want to bang your head on the wall.

DEI hire. Clueless. Class is a complete waste of time. After 4-5 weeks of listening to him, I decided to sit outside the classroom, with dozens of other students, check in for the attendance credit, then immediately leave. Rivals Jay Johnson for the worst hire in the history of Michigan State University.

First mistake, I ignored RMP. There is no way on EARTH that this man has any formal education or merit to be a professor. 1/4 of the lecture is him victimizing himself, 2/4 is him being passive aggressive, 3/4 is him complaining, 4/4 is his long pauses. If you try to ask for feedback on a project he will act like you insulted his family. Fire him.

Lazy and had to let dean officials know
- 3 heavy assignments and graded them after the semester ended but also made mandatory attendance (Leaving students in the dark, also does not follow his syllabus) 
- Emails go unanswered and excuses it for having 500 students 
- No rubrics for grading and doesn't discuss feedback 
Wont have a job in 5 years

analysis.name: Clifford Broman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Broman is a good professor and his lectures are super interesting. The class is pretty difficult with a lot of pre-class readings & the tests are almost entirely based on the readings. He does give a lot of extra credit, usually attendance. It was hard but I don't regret taking it at all, he really teaches you things you've never learned before

He's very knowledgable. I learned a lot in this class, and he makes it very clear that if you don't go to class, you won't do well. I agree because this class is very lecture heavy, but the slides are easy to follow. I didn't do the readings and still did fine. Just put SOME effort in and you'll be fine.

As a freshman, this quickly became the class I dreaded most on Mondays and Wednesdays. Professor Broman does nothing but sit on his chair and read word by word from the extremely outdated powerpoint. His exams are extremely difficult for no reason, and he does not give back graded assignments, so I guessed my grade until the end of the semester.

The professor was amazing and super funny. However, you must write three 20+ page summaries based on 80+ chapters throughout the semester, which only count for 5 points. Exams are long, detailed, and mostly textbook-based. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he offers random extra credit for showing up. Thought others were exaggerating, but trust them.
all im gonna say is don't take this class, take literally any other class for your own future sanity. its interesting, but all that comes with this class is not worth it.

analysis.name: Blair  Burnette
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Burnette is AWESOME and would recommend her class to everyone. She is very knowledgeable and is super interested in hearing students' responses to class material. Lectures were very engaging, and there are only a few assignments even graded for accuracy- the other ones are just graded for completion. You get 1 drop each assignment as well.

Dr. Burnette is amazing. Simple assignments throughout the semester, and you get drops for everything. 5 pop quizzes but besides that attendance is not mandatory. Her lectures were always entertaining and she had guest speakers for every topic. So much extra credit! She is one of the nicest profs I had and this was an easy, informative class.

I would take every single psychology class with Dr. Burnette if I could. She is genuinely the best professor I've ever had. She is so knowledgeable and encourages class discussion and is open to all questions. Every assignment gets at least 1 drop, goes for quizzes as well. Class material is so interesting as well.

This class was so easy, and genuinely so fun and interesting. Attendance is not required, but I still looked forward to going because the class is amazing. I would 10/10 recommend Dr. Burnette. She does use IClicker, Pop quizzes, and online assignments, but overall this class is an EXTREMELY EASY 4.0.

genuinely one of the best psych classes ive taken. dr. burnette is fantastic and the lectures are really well done and make class very interesting. i always looked forward to her class. all you have is weekly homework (which is straightforward and very manegabkle) and few exams. would highly reccomend!

analysis.name: Shlagha Borha
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Good class with easy assignments, but gets cancelled all. the. time. it became disorganized quickly and confusing to stay on track with deadlines because class was cancelled so often.

She was a good person, but the amount of times she cancelled class last minute was wild. Because my class was an 8:00 am, there was over ten times where I would be in the classroom and we would get an email saying class was cancelled, a few times even after class had started. The class itself was very disorganized, mostly due to many cancellations.

If you're into creative work and open to learn new perspectives, take this class! She is fun, caring, and despite some of the students making this class difficult for her because of circumstances unrelated to the class, she is empathetic and a kind grader. I loved her!

She cancels all the time very last minute so don't take an 8 am class with her. Her class is very easy. She will make you read outload sometimes and work in groups or partners. All work is easy and there is never homework.

The professor is not all that bad. the class is easy and the writing assignments are not hard. For me, she did not come off as rude or have a bad attitude. She did however cancel class last minute a LOT or change it to Zoom that was extremely annoying. there is also a lot of reading in class and group discussions

analysis.name: David Bramer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 146 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He spends a good majority of the lecture making you work on your own which is difficult to do since you haven't learned the  material yet. It's also very hard to understand what he's doing considering he jumps around the notes and rarely finishes a problem. He refuses to give you answers on anything because "struggling is learning"

I can tell you wholeheartedly that David Bramer is beyond a doubt the most useless professor I have ever had in my entire life. Half of the lecture is spent on your own trying to do math that he hasn't taught yet. Isn't lecture supposed to be where he shows you examples for later use? I only 3.0'd the class because of the MLC. Lecture was useless.

Bramer is a great guy and his lectures are helpful and he will answer any question. Recitations are very dependent on TA. Webwork is easy and you get 3 tries so good grades always. Quiz and tests are quite difficult and often graded harshly. Put in the effort and take some time out of class to actually learn the stuff and you'll get a good grade

This class wasn't too bad. To me, I think he gives good lectures and its easy to stay focused when you're taking notes and asking questions.GO TO THE MATH LEARNING CENTER. It's hit or miss on tutors but I had some amazing ones at Brody and they helped me so much on webwork and studying for tests. All tests and quizes are online with lockdown

His lectures are VERY confusing and like other students noted on here, he goes through the material expecting you already have some understanding of it and it is very hard to focus. He goes very fast through lecture and skips around in the notes making it very confusing. Homework is very easy for the class but it is NOTHING like the exams at all.

analysis.name: David Barondess
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Barondess is a nice guy and good to get along with. Unfortunately, his exams a written pretty poorly and many questions do not make much sense. This is difficult because exams and quizzes make up the entire grade. He also tends to ramble during lecture so it is difficult to tell whether he is lecturing or talking just to talk.

Dr. Barondess is a good guy, but, unfortunately, his exams are so heavy, and that's all you get graded on + quizzes. He also rambles on a lot, so it's hard to tell whether he's going on a tangent or whether you'll be tested on it.

If you're a student that puts in an average amount of effort by going to lectures and actively listening, you will be fine. All content is covered in lectures, and grading based on 6 quizzes + 4 exams. First few weeks of learning statistic interpretation is boring but after that it gets interesting. The reviews made me nervous, but he was great!

If you go to class, listen, and put in effort, you'll do well. Students who rated him poorly likely lack sufficient attention span and discipline. Dr. Barondess does ramble sometimes, but what he says is relevant to course content, which is straightforward and interesting for people who pursuing careers medicine and public health.

Do not listen to the hateful reviews. Insanely helpful outside of class, lectures are easy to follow even for someone with ADHD, and the class is very interesting. The workload/tests/quizzes are very manageable but hard if you don't pay attention. I've written some awful reviews on here but this guy does not deserve the hate he has.

analysis.name: Carmen Octavio
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO.NOT.TAKE.HER. Has no clear instructions and its a teach your own class. This is based off of homework and says it is based off completion when it is truly based on correctness.  She says you get three excused absences, but only marks participation as grading, so basically you can not miss a single class. I advise you drop the class if signed up

Very direct and can have an attitude. Classes consist of mostly answering HW questions, which wasn't helpful as little time was left for lecture slides. Grading is REALLY tough and instructions can be unclear. However, HW is a big part of your grade which can cover up a bad exam. Very accessible outside class and helpful feedback.
Seems like a nice person, but I find the class to be mind-numbing. Expect to learn the material on your own time because the whole class time is taken up reviewing the homework from the day before.

This professor does not help you learn anything. She instead uses her time to send multiple emails out to students accusing them of using AI. Multiple people have now dropped the course due to fears of them receiving an academic dishonesty report, even if they didn't use AI... Adding to that, her D2L is not set up correctly. Do NOT TAKE HER !!!!!!!

I was terrified to take her summer SPN202 course after reading the reviews. Her character is blunt and to the point — I believe this is where majority of the bad reviews are coming from. She is, however, an incredible teacher with effective curricula. Her class was challenging, but was the one I improved in most out of the four SPN classes I took.

analysis.name: Chuck Fessler
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very passive-aggressive when asking questions, almost rude even. Not good at teaching and with the most unclear grading criteria possible. I legit couldn't see my percent grade all semester. Expect lots of meaningless group projects and busy work. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy, but oftentimes hard to understand. Do not take.

I took LB 117 online, for the most part it was the same content as my high school calculus class but he either never elaborated on what he wanted us to do on the labs, or briefly went over what material he wanted us to turn in and always took so long to grade stuff. Overall horrible experience.

horrible horrible horrible never ever take mth103 with chuck fessler. he may be the worst teacher i've ever had in my entire life. his grading doesn't make any sense, the exams do not correlate with the material we learn in class whatsoever and he does not respond well to criticism or feedback and blames everyone failing on us not being prepared.

A nice guy to talk to, but awful teacher. Does not give any instructions and expects you to know everything before hand. Does not grade until the last minute and does not grade resubmits fast, so you don't know what you get wrong.

I took calc in high school, and struggled with his class. He does not explain well, and examples we do in class are completely different than assessments. I turned in an assignment in the beginning of October and it was not graded until early December. It was also nearly impossible to tell what your actual grade was throughout. not a good time

Lectures are not mandatory but you WONT pass this class without continued attendance and detailed notes. Would take again.

Super knowledgeable, probably more than most professors in her field. That being said, GO TO CLASS!! The exams are almost entirely based on class discussions. The lecture slides barely help and the textbook is basically your only option. The homework is chill but can take a very long time. Can be passive-aggressive if you ask dumb questions.

Professor Fenn was very thorough and outlined all expectations of the course. There is research included so be sure to get this done on time! Generous curves are provided and overall it is easy to succeed. Going to lectures are important and the course is test heavy---but there is a drop and a final will replace lowest score.

Dr. Fenn is a great lecturer and definitely knows her stuff. However, you can tell that she dislikes her life.  She is extremely hot and cold towards students. One moment she will be nice and the next she will lash out at you with no warning. I would avoid her if given the chance. Also expect rude emails and responses if you ask questions.

Make sure to attend class and take notes! The exams are based on lectures, the slides will not help you, attendance is not mandatory so don't let that tempt you. There is Inquisitive homework due every Friday night which is easy. Part of your grade is from research hours, and extra credit will be available to you.

analysis.name: LaVelle Gipson-Tansil
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I usually don't write, but I had to this time. When someone asked for feedback, she said it was too much work. When I asked to make up a quiz the next week, she said yes, but when the it came she ignored all my chats and emails. When someone asked how to get graded, she put it in the chat for everyone to see. Grading is also bad.

Her grading system is ridiculous, she barely gives out extra credit even though on D2L there are lots of extra credit opportunities listed, and the lectures are so long me and several of my classmates fell asleep.

If you want to pass this class, here is a tip. when answering the field assignments, write essay length answers (or a large paragraph).

Worst professor at MSU. She will give you points to act like "you're earning points" until the final test comes around, you get a terrible grade for no reason. I don't understand her thought process when she grades. I think she just wants to give people a bad score for fun. Thought about switching my major a couple times, if that says anything!!

Terrible communicator. I emailed her so many times over the semester begging to get assignments graded that I completed on time, it took her months. She constantly posted wrong dates on D2L and never corrected them, leaving everyone so stressed. The class was very boring, she just reads the slides and then ends class with a NEVER ENDING WORKLOAD.

She had the dates on the quizzes wrong and I could not take them. She took a month to fix it and I had to take all the past quizzes in one day. She is a super harsh grader and does not explain why she took off points. She assigned about 15 pages of reading each week along with about 3 assignments a week plus a quiz. A 95% is 4.0 and a 70% is a 1.0.

analysis.name: John Grey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you don't know anything about philosophy this class can be difficult. He does make you buy a textbook but it helps with understanding the texts and you can use it on exams. You aren't graded on a lot: 2 midterms, a final, and random in-class activities to get you in class. But Dr. Grey is amazing, would take his class again in a heartbeat.

One of my favorite classes that I have taken! Dr. Grey knows his stuff and is willing to answer anything you throw at him. Weekly papers, but: Go. To. Class. Not only will this help you understand the content better, but he does random in-class activities which can help your grade. Not a Philosophy major but I will be taking more of his classes.

Don't take this class. He doesn't teach you anything more than the 274-page book does, along with the 4 other books in the class. You can't use outside resources to study because it's so based on niche books. He has 2 exams covering 60% of your grade. Also, the recitation pretty much exists solely to turn in your homework. Do not take this class...

Dr. Grey is an amazing professor and knows what he is lecturing on, attendance is mandatory (especially for reviews before exams) if you want to receive a good grade in this class. Annotations every week which are about 1 page and are easy to write and definitely help you understand the material better, and he hand grades each one with feedback. :)

Lectures are pretty boring, but if you're into sentience/consciousness topics you might still find the material interesting. Grading feels harsh, a 91% is only a 3.5 and you can't make up missed in-class assignments. Overall, interesting content but not the most engaging class or flexible policies.

analysis.name: Sarah Griffes
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sarah is so kind. Her passion for teaching really comes through, making lectures engaging and enjoyable. She's always open to questions. Quizzes are taken online without proctoring, and exams can be done from your dorm with a camera + mic on. You'll have discussions and engagement activities, but you're given at least two weeks, sometimes a month.

She's the sweetest! Her lectures were so engaging, I always looked forward to the days she was lecturing. I preferred her to the actual professor, and you can tell she has so much passion for the topic. I would take her class every semester if I could. Love her.

I loved her so much. So easy to talk to and ready to have a conversation due to her passion of the topics. My only complaint is the sort of bias she has on some of the subjects which I am unsure if it's related to ciriculm guide or her opinion. Overall, I would recommend this professor and course to all students

This class was awesome, super easy to follow and actually interesting to learn about. Such a great professor and I truly recommend this class to anyone. Attendance is taken randomly using iclicker. You have an assignment every week, but they're short. Final was a paper and wasn't bad to write at all. She's always helpful and answers all questions.

Prof Griffes was a great professor! There were only two assignments weekly and usually a biweekly reading quiz, but you get access to your book and it's super easy. She likes class engagement, and attendance is mandatory through iclicker. Only three or four tests I believe and you can take them in person or at your dorm w a camera on. Great teacher

analysis.name: George Harnick
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy! The class was very easy, and there were only 4 assignments the whole time. Guys, please laugh at his joke of the day it makes me sad when people don't! Kinda quirky, but a very passionate teacher and someone who would help you in the future in a heartbeat.
Such an amazing professor! Genuinely made every lecture so engaging and enjoyable. He is so funny and goes out of his way to accommodate and help students, could not recommend him enough!!

My favorite professor by far! He truly cares, adds humor to keep lectures engaging, makes students comfortable asking questions, and is always responsive to emails, even if you're a former student. He truly helped me love the class and want to be there and engaged. You have to write your name on a piece of paper when you go, but it's not mandatory.

George is one of my absolute favorite professors. Super engaging with the students and genuinely cares about his students' learning. You'll have to study for his exams but nothing too difficult. Also a little bit of homework but totally managable
He is the best. He is so nice and funny. He genuinely cared about each student. The class was so easy too.

analysis.name: Gary Topolewski
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He always knows how to make the assignments fun and interesting. He doesn't have monologue lectures. He plants seeds of creativity and lets students brainstorm and sprout that creativity. Mostly conceptual than detailed.

Gary is such a kind professor. I took ADV210 with him and it was the easiest class ever. Weekly group projects on concept development, 2 weeks per project, easily accessible outside of class and accommodating. Easy grader, just put in the work!

This is my third course with Gary and he is BY FAR the best, most genuine and caring professor I have had at my time during MSU. Great feedback and is super knowledgeable. He's a great professor but an even better person.

HE IS the most understanding and caring human EVER. Most of the class is small assignments that you present. He gives great feedback on what you did well and didn't, so on. He doesn't post in D2L though. PLEASE take him if you can/have to. Great guy and good to have in your life. Attendance is encouraged since that's where assignments are discussed
He is one of the most laid back professors I've ever had at MSU. He is extremely flexible with due dates and is really passionate about what he teaches.

analysis.name: Najib Hourani
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: ISS 320 consists of three exams, 1 extra credit opportunity for 5 points (usually a random lecture midday on a weekday) Exams are poorly written, shows up late, gives indirect answers to questions, and studying effectively is nearly impossible because he doesn't post slides. Goes on unrelated political rants. Exams are opinion-based, not an easy A.

Not enough grading opportunities to accurately judge a student's ability on the subject at hand. His lectures also follow a random pattern with no chance to study correctly due to his lack of assignments and withholding proper study materials, such as the slides.

I took ISS 320 with him. The class itself was about "urban planning." However, rarely have we talked about any cities, and when we did, we only talked about Arab cities. He has mentioned several times how he is from Lebannon and that is mostlyall we learned about: Lebannon and the Arab world. Only grades are 3 very difficult exams. I HATE HIM!

I took his class based on the reviews here and he is a good teacher but he is kind of a dictator in the class. He gives lots of reading and you have to be ready for class discussions, the first exam was easy but the ones after that were hard. All I can say is keep up with the readings and GO to class most of the exams are from class discussion.

I was so surprised to see negative reviews on Dr. Hourani. He was truly one of my favorite professors, and while his classes are reading heavy, he is very patient and understanding. If you make an effort and have open communication with him about any problems, you will do well in this class. He is engaging and makes the class feel connected.

analysis.name: Valerie Hedges
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: So kind and easy to reach through email. Wants everyone to succeed, and easy to 4.0 if you come to class and watch the lecture videos. She is very knowledgeable and helpful if you have questions. She makes this class run very well and it is not a class I ever worry about. Lockdown exams with no camera too and other assignments boosting your grade.

The flipped classroom style isn't for me, but Prof. Hedges was great. Her assignments are very interesting, and you can attend classes in-person OR online (Zoom). Do the study guides, keep up with assignments, and learn the content well- you will get a 4.0. One tip: Make sure you have a good grasp of the material. Tests are application-heavy.

Dr. Hedges was amazing. This class was super helpful to my learning and it was relatively easy to get a good grade as long as you did the assignments and understood how to do the exams. The class is hybrid which is nice if you can't make it. Be sure to do the in-class assignments and weekly quizzes and you will be able to 4.0 this course.

Dr. Hedges is very willing to work with you, and she provides a lot of course materials for you to understand the material. I didn't do too well, but looking back on it, this is only because I was stressed with many other difficult classes. Dr. Hedges gives amazing feedback, make sure to attend class and office hours!!

best professor ive had in all my 3 years. i have never learned as difficult information and actually understood it as quickly as i have in this class due to the way this class is formatted. i got the highest grades on everything without having to study once.

analysis.name: Harish Sankaranarayanan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He uses tophat for attendance which you can do remotely. Overall if you attend lectures and recitation, understanding the content is really easy. Exams are a huge portion of the grade so you have to prepare for them. There's some extra credit built into the homework too.

Dr.H is funny, and stays after class to help people and is open to it. I asked to talk with him because I missed due to illness and he said no, thought that was weird but otherwise chill and communicating through email. I failed the class but I'd def take Dr.H again!

He was a great stats professor. If you go to recitation and go to class everyday, you will do great! One thing that annoyed me was him letting people go early which was super distracting to people like me who stayed all of class. Overall, super easy math requirement with only 3 exams and a lot of extra credit offered to bump your grade 2.5%.

Going to class is important because its easy to fall behind. Lots of extra credit. If you show up to lectures and recitations and do your homework and extra credit you will be fine. Tough grader however, Would not round me up .2 to next highest grade which was frustrating but like i said there is a lot of extra credit opportunities getting me close

Dr. H was a very nice and friendly man, but I felt like his lectures were too fast paced and at times he didn't fully explain the material. I would go to study for exams and would teach myself the whole exam material the week before the test. The content was not difficult it just took time to learn. There are many resources to get help such as SLC.

analysis.name: Kathleen Hoag
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty standard freshmen seminar class for BLD students. Attendance is mandatory but the class meets once a week for 50 minutes so it isn't super demanding. I honestly did not buy the books but instead read them online but if you miss a reading it is not a big deal. The exam is not difficult, and neither is the class. She keeps it real.

This course was very test heavy but as long as you study the Learning Objectives you will pass very helpful for questions but the sheer intensity of so much content can make the course difficult if you don't invest enough time into the course which is stressed on by the professor. She seems to love the field and constantly updating the class.

It is graded on case studies and section quizzes. To be quite honest, focus well on the learning objectives and it will be fine. Some of the material is difficult, but many of the facilitators were helpful and so was Dr. Hoag. study well and you will be fine.

Dr. Hoag is a good professor at heart, but she heavily relies on you to do your part as a student. If you are looking into graduate school, she does help prepare you. She is not easy whatsoever and there are times where you may feel frustrated, but she does it out of good intent of making you into a smarter and more dilligent student overall.
She's definitely strict, but I enjoyed this class and thought she did a great job teaching.

analysis.name: Nathan Haut
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: GIVE THIS MAN A RAISE!!! Content & exams are seriously tough, but most of the grade comes from pre class & in class assignments & the project. Show up every day and you'll do great. Dr Haut is an amazing & chill guy who TRULY cares about his students (more than any prof I've ever had). I highly recommend him and getting to know him in this course!

so nice & genuine! really thorough w answering questions, i had a great experience w this class even as someone that doesn't like cs :) one thing is that the ML unit is quite hard, and it's common to not finish the in-class activities (although they are graded for completion). the exams are lowkey rough but they're not heavily weighted.

Anyone who rates him poorly probably never asked him a content question. He will sit with you and help you through your work. His explanations are clear and he is very thorough in his descriptions of the content. Very kind and engaging guy.
Super smart guy. Will give you high-quality detailed advice so make sure you pay attention.
Super hardass over a 2 hundred level course.

analysis.name: Joseph Hefner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, Doctor Hefner is AMAZING. If you do your homework, study, and go to lecture there is no way you would not be able to 4.0 this class. Also, just be honest with him he is so accommodating. He enjoys what he does and he loves teaching/talking to the class. The only way to fail this class is on your end, he wants you to succeed. TRUST ME.

(ANP441) Dr. Hefner was an amazing prof. Took the class for an Hbio selective and loved it! He's very understanding, caring, and easy to reach. Gave pretty clear study guides before the exams and lots of extra credit! I hadn't taken an anp class before and had no issues. Go to lecture and study the bones/ their characteristics and you can 4.0!

Teaches anthropology and made it fun! Exams are a little difficult but if you study and go through the study guide as well as some of the topics/practice questions from the smartbook you will do well. It is more lecture heavy but the content taught was not boring because he didnt make it boring.

His class was very interesting, and he was a really great professor overall. Make sure you go to every class; he gives extra credit, which lets you skip the final at the end. However, his exams are worth a lot, so I recommend taking many notes during his lectures and reading the book.
He was a very chill professor. He just requires attendance to do well as the lectures aren't typically posted. If you go to class you can easily 4.0.

analysis.name: Thomas Hamann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It's a very difficult class, but he is a very good teacher and passionate to teach. It is quite test heavy and be ready to study a lot, but he's really qualified to teach it and explains it to the best of his ability

Professor Hamann is a nice guy, and he seems to genuinely care about the course and the people taking it. However, he isn't always very clear, and a lot of the time, when asked a question in lecture, he would give a kind of non-answer that wasn't too helpful. The class itself wasn't too bad as long as you keep up, but it's very test-heavy.

This class made me want to jump into the Red Cedar. The assigned chapters and office hours are necessary for comprehension but honestly make a study group if you want to pass the exams. The class average for most exams was around 60% and the curve applies after the final. He starts out with quantum mechanics so be prepared. Good luck
CEM 181H is a tough class, but he does his best to make it accessible. A lot of self study because homework is light.
He is a shy professor, but very passionate, but he is too shy that sometimes he is not very helpful

analysis.name: LaShawn Harris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The course material was very interesting, and the readings required for each class were interesting and the content was expanded upon in lecture. Biweekly writing assignments were short and helped with my comprehension of the reading, and her feedback was very helpful.

Harris was such a nice lady. At first, the material might seem like a lot and the pretty much all written exams might seem overwhelming, but she tells you exactly what she wants you to know for the exams. I hate reading and barely skimmed for her class and still did well. You do have to go to class though, but she lets you miss 3 classes

Dr. Harris is a very intelligent and interesting lecturer. I found tests pretty easy but there was a lot of writing. 3 books but you really only had to read the one for the final paper. She is really good at facilitating conversation and I learned a lot from this course.

Dr. Harris is a great professor. She is very flexible and understanding. The material in class is very much interesting and you learn so much every class period. She loves engaging with her students during lectures. Exams are not hard because she gives out study guides with all the material you should know. I got a 3.0 and I almost failed 2/4 exams

I loved her class! I thought she had really awesome lectures that were interesting and informative. The tests were very to the point and she didn't try and trick us on any questions which was fair. I really had a good experience in her class.

analysis.name: Sadam Issa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Sadam is one of the best teachers at Michigan State. Arabic is a difficult language to learn, but his teaching methods are unmatched. Be sure to do the homework and required readings, he will be sure to tell you he's disappointed if you do not. Super caring guy, and attendance matters to him the most.

One of if not the best teacher I've ever had. He takes something as difficult as Arabic and somehow makes it easy to learn, and is engaging at the same time. This is the kind of class where you have to want to get better at, but the prof gives you the resources to be very successful. also he is hilarious

One of my favorite professors. Very effective at teaching Arabic, but if you don't actually want to learn, don't take him because you will fail. If you care about the language and the material and you put in the work to learn a second language, he will help you succeed. Also he's hilarious.
A really nice professor and was very interesting to listen to! Lots of participation needed in class and must attend all classes. He was very fun and easy to talk to and get to know.
Class was easy, but never graded my final and other assignments even after emailing him and talking to him in person. Assignments were turned in on time and done correctly

analysis.name: Irma Bartolo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is not that bad. Sometimes she can be a little unclear or confusing, but overall it doesn't really matter since she grades so easily. Like a month into the class she started saying we can just talk in English for most discussions so that we can have better comprehension. She's also pretty kind and funny.

She's not as bad as the other reviews say, but she's definitely not great. Her class is pretty tough and there is a lot of online homework and participation is required for every class, but she's pretty leinent on grading essays, assignments, and there's no proper tests. She can be a little bit rude, but will give you help if you ask for it.

Definitely the worst spanish professor I have had here. She is unclear with directions, not understanding of personal life events, and makes fun of her students when they mess up pronunciation or spelling. She does not make learning this language enjoyable. I have considered no longer minoring in spanish because of her. Do not recommend.

This professor caused a lot of stress and frustration for me and my peers. She was very unclear about expectations during class time and would frequently make people feel uncomfortable by singling people out for not understanding what she thought was basic knowledge. She would also make fun of/mock our language skills and culture.

Easily the worst Spanish teacher I've had. She was consistently passive aggressive and abrasive with students and always had a condescending tone. She also often contradicts her own directions and is super unorganized.The class was easy but I learned so much more from things I did on my own outside of the curriculum. I do not recommend her.

analysis.name: Ilse Schweitzer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was such a sweet professor, very organized and clear. Pretty homework heavy because of the 5 papers written over the semester, but she does try to give you as much work time and flexibility as possible. Overall the class was enjoyable, and she is very easy to talk to.

All around great professor. Super nice and lectures are interesting. I really enjoyed WRA 101 with professor Schweitzer. The semester consists of 5 projects and are relatively easy and manageable. The final is just a reflection essay.

Dr. Isle is sweet. I have bad anxiety but she doesn't randomly call on someone to answer. If nobody answers she just answers herself (THANK GOD)! Since this is a writing class prepare to write tons of essay's. Overall it's an easy class because you can write whatever you want.

Ilse's WRA101 was an easy and sometimes even fun class, you do 4 projects over the semester but you are given a ton of time to do them as well as peer review phases. Ilse is also very kind to the class and an approachable person. The lessons were fun and interesting as well (especially the conspiracies one!) and we visited a few places on campus.
She is the sweetest. 4 main assignments are essays so prepare to write about anything you like.

analysis.name: Iglika Pavlova
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had her for BS 162 + BS 191H. I can confidently say that she is a fantastic professor and very caring. In BS 191H, she gives tons of feedback and really wants you to do well and understand. Now, BS 162 was genuinely one of the worst classes I have ever taken; however, its MSUs flawed curriculum, not her "lack of expertise." Take 162 at community.

Going into lectures was just a waste of my time, we didn't learn anything and she just gave us busy work. She isn't very good at teaching. All class lectures was online that you had to watch before class. The exams are half online (proctored) and half in person, they were pretty hard. If you have a background in bio then you will be fine.

In my opinion, the professor is very wholesome. She deeply cares about students. The thing is, this class has tons ( REALLY A LOT ) of assignments, and missing a few affects grade by a significant percent. Moreover, Dr. P speaks in between in class assignments and Iclicker, sometimes, which kinda makes it difficult to focus in class.

This is the worst set up class I have ever taken. All learning is done by yourself, outside of class. Class time is reserved for group work with people who don't even show up and when they do, no one knows what's going on so it's the blind leading the blind. There're 8 million worksheets to complete. Just thinking about this class infuriates me.

I had high hopes for this class. This is a confusing class, the lectures are all online and when we go in person we don't really learn anything. She is very kind and knows what she is talking about, she just can't explain it. There is a lot of other stuff in the class that helps your grade so it is hard to fail.

analysis.name: Iliya  Miralavykomsari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Miralavy has been assigned to restructure and teach most of CSE232, and thank god for that. He has completely swept in and saved this course from the depths of hell. Miralavy is an amazing professor and lecturer, everything is very clear, and is just all around a great guy. If you have the chance to take any of his courses, do it.

Professor Miralavykomsari is amazing. Aside from being a super nice person, He's also has passion and is knows a lot about the topics. Grading is projects and exams. As long as you pay attention in lecture and review the slides then you'll be set for the exam. Projects are slightly covered in lectures, But they may take more time than expected.

OH I hate him. He is not undeerstanding at all. He doesn't even know the course policies of his class. He is not what is seems like in the class. Very reluctant to help in the name of "being fair to other kids"
Truly one of the all time GOATS. You are lucky if you happen to get him. Cares about his students. If you go to office hours he WILL go out of his way to help.

analysis.name: Brooke Ingersoll
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ingersoll is the platonic ideal of a professor, role model, and citizen. Sometimes—if you're lucky enough—you have the privilege of spending time in the company of a truly great mind. She is a genius. Nay—a visionary.  She slays. She sashays. She commits to the bit.

This was an extremely hard class and Dr. Ingersoll made it impossible to do well in it. She was not concerned with how terrible the class as a whole would do on exams and blamed it on our poor study habits. The study guides were so long it was impractical for the students to know all the material. I wish I didn't take this class for my PSYW credit

Lectures were online and when we had to come to class once a week we basically did nothing. Exams were difficult but she was generous with the curve on the midterm. Lectures went into tons of detail and exam questions were really specific (barely any guidance for studying). Loved her as a person (very sweet) but disliked structure of the class.

This was the worst professor I have had in Psychology. Her mentality is that there's nothing wrong with her tests, the students just need to study harder. The tests were impossible and made up a large part of your grade and the literature review was extremely hard to do well on. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
Dr. Ingersoll is great. She is incredibly passionate about her job and that shows in her lectures. She also gives great feedback on papers.

analysis.name: S. Kutnjak Ivkovic
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall good professor who cares a lot about class engagement. There are in person checks (10 of them) but homework isnt too bad and exams are online but are proctored. Not that hard of a class if you make somewhat of an effort.
Not a fan, lockdown browser tests that record you. Exam questions poorly worded and makes the exam harder than it should be. Pop quizzes for attendance.

I absolutely adored Professor K! She genuinely cares about her students, and she wants everyone in the class to absorb as much as possible. She asks for a lot of answers from the class, and interacts with everyone during the entire lecture. She makes clear power points, and posts everything before class starts. Loved her!

Best prof ive had so far for criminal justice. Her material was interesting and she kept it engaging. Her exams were based off the study guides, as long as you paid attention in class youd get 100%. Passed all exams and homework. Attendance is mandatory, but you can get excused if good reasoning. 10/10 would take again!

Take notes during her lectures and use that to double with her slides while studying. She uses her own version of her slides to base her exams. She appreciates participation and will ask frequent questions about the slides and she goes through them. Pay attention and study for the exams and you will have no problem.

analysis.name: Ignat Soroko
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best teacher, and easy to pass
