Finish the ALEKS 100% before the deadline and the class should be a decently easy pass. Not super accommodating past the allotted absences so save them for emergencies. Lectures were actually helpful and I highly recommend going, even if you don't have to. If you survived AP Chem, it's basically a guaranteed 2.0. Chemistry is awful, she's great!

She posts Lecture Slide videos so if you need to review these are very helpful, Do your ALEKS as soon as possible! She seems snarky at times,sometimes she'll be like "I can't answer that, but a TA can." with a sarcastic smile. This can be frustrating. She also has an accent that isn't too hard to understand but definitely has you listening closer.

(Taken Spring 2023) 

Good lecturer, can sometimes go a little fast but is very nice with clear explanations. Her exams are easy to score high on if you follow along with the material intently. The people who scored poorly didn't study well or didn't care to set time aside to actually learn the material.

She is very smart and very kind. You can tell she just wants the best for her students. If you ask her questions she is always happy to help and is accessible outside lecture. She does have an accent but that shouldn't stop you from taking her class, as she does a very good job explaining difficult concepts. I found 142 to be much easier than 141.

analysis.name: Zenaida Moreno Mosqueda
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Moreno is very sweet and kind, and open to discussing social justice issues today. She is also very funny and loves to tell stories. This class is very writing-heavy, so just be prepared. She can be a harsh grader, but she does give good feedback so that you can get a good grade on the final draft. Overall, an amazing professor personally.

She was funny and nice to talk to, but was difficult when it came to grading. You need to be participating a lot during each class as she will take away points every lecture if not. The essays are worth 50% of your grade and the 2 tests had no study guide and we had no idea what would be on them. When I was sick I could not make up work missed

Professor Moreno Mosqueda was the worst professor I've experienced at MSU and many other people in our class agreed. It was almost impossible to get a 4.0 in her class unless you are a native Spanish speaker. She graded so harshly and then offered no further help or feedback. She was rude at times and very inaccessible outside of class for help.

Absolutely dreaded this class every week because of her. Consistently complained about her job, was impossible to reach via email and for office hours, and docked attendance points even if you participated and were paying attention. Showed no understanding for her students, lacked professionalism, and was condescending and rude multiple times.

Overall, the class content was not difficult. Her grading was harsh and she was condescending. For a language class, we should be given room to learn from our mistakes and improve them. However, Professor Moreno is unforgiving. Did not seem like she cared.

analysis.name: Mohamed Satti
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would recommend going to one of his office hours to introduce yourself or ask questions, he's a really nice guy to talk to. I would not say that this class has a heavy workload. We usually had 1-2 assignments a week along with some reading. Lectures are easy to understand and the exams are directly from learning actives in class.

You're on your own in this course. Despite emailing Professor Satti for help multiple times throughout the semester, his responses were short and sharp, and it is clear that he is unfit to be teaching an asynchronous class.

While this class is all online, Dr. Satti was truly a great professor. Many of the aspects of this course are outside of his control, however, when asking for clarification or you need a better understanding of the content, he truly was knowledgeable and cared about whether you understood the concept. Strongly recommend Dr. Satti!

Get ready to question your sanity as you embark on the horrendous journey of PH101. You will spend hours every day if you wish to do the required readings (which you should take notes on if you are seeking a good grade on quizzes and assignments) and trying to complete some very complicated writing assignments. You will be so frustrated every week.

So my roomie took this course, and bro legit stole her from me. They were losing sleep trying to put in the most insane amount of time ever requested by a teacher for a non-honours, online 100 level course (literally multiple hours a day). It's absurd. They read this whack book that had some really disturbing content and no content warning???

analysis.name: Mariana Medina
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Medina is kind and cares about her students. This class was easy, and as long as you showed up to recitation, you could get a great grade on every assignment. No final or midterms. Although reading was required, it wasn't necessary to excel in the course. Great professor, and would be happy to take another one of her classes!

You could tell Dr. Medina was very interested in the subject matter, and knew a lot about it, so this made asking her questions or whatnot a lot easier. You're only graded by a few things, but she makes the grading criteria very flexible, and she's a pretty easy grader. Definitely take the honors section if you need an honors credit!

Take this professor if you can! She is very nice and caring! Grades are comprised of weekly assignments that you do in the recitation and attendance, so no exams or anything. The class was super easy, and make sure to go to the recitation! Really nice prof, great at helping with honors credit as well!

Objectively easy course. The lectures are boring but there's no exams, you just need to show up for attendance, and you can skim the powerpoint to get an easy 3.0+. She's very understanding and the absence policy is pretty lenient. Great GPA boost/course to add onto a busy schedule. Would take again!

Great prof who really cares about her students! Attendance policy is super lenient, and I found that it wasn't hard to catch up if you missed class. Quizzes were all open-book, open-lecture and open-note (I got a 4.0 just from Ctrl + F searching key terms), and there are no midterms or finals -- your entire grade is 20% attendance, 80% quizzes.

analysis.name: Nicole Mccleese
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: McCleese only gave out 5 assignments the whole semester.  She takes attendance randomly so just attend even though it is boring af. Her lessons are so boring, playing minesweeper is more entertaining. She reads everything off of a slideshow, (which that is NOT posted to D2L).

Slow grades (no grades entered more than halfway through the semester), and the course topic is just not what the class is described as. If you want to learn more about Chilean politics, def take this course, but if you're looking for reading writing by women, this isn't it.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. I was expecting the course to relate to the description MSU put out, but she put an "indigenous food studies" twist to it. Lectures consist of her reading slides in a monotone voice. She gives us useless assingments and hasn't graded anything the entire semester (less than a month left). Stay away.

Very careless about student feedback or incidents. Took random attendance for the first month as a scare tactic, then suddenly stopped, nobody knows when she will take attendance next. If you are absent, she gives 0 grace to your situation regardless of how serious. She has a temper, and petty mannerisms. There's not much work she gives out.

This professor graded everything a week before the course ended. An okay instructor who oddly made the class about food culture. Assignments were easy ten-minute tasks, with only five total grades, so submit on time. Attendance wasn't taken, so skipping didn't matter. Clear grading, but never replied to emails.

analysis.name: Stephanie Nawyn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Nawyn's lectures. She's funny and explains terms/theories well. She has online open note exams, weekly readings, and iclicker quizzes, but they're fairly easy if you read the textbook and pay attention in class. Would 100% recommend taking SOC 100 with her!

All exams are open note/book, super easy class overall and hard not to 4.0! Lectures can be long/boring, she tends to get off task. The sweetest professor-intelligent, understanding, down to earth, absolutely hilarious. She wants everyone to succeed. I wish I could get coffee with her. Couldn't recommend enough!

Such a wonderful professor to have. She is educated, thoughtful, passionate, and caring to her students. She truly does care, and you can just tell. There were five exams, with the final, and one can be dropped. All are open note, and most were taken online, with an in-person option. No reason not to take a class with such a wonderful person :)

I love Prof Nawyn. There are iclicker questions and daily quizzes but they are easy as long as you do the readings which are a little long but its fine. Inquisitives were annoying but easy points. Very fun and followable lectures, shes funny here and there too. Very accommodating and there are many points in the class. Easy exams w a note card.

This is the easiest class I have taken. The lectures are important to go to for extra credit, lecture points and for exam material. There is so much extra credit given that I had 20 points of extra credit over the maximum points available in the class. You get a cheat sheet on the test and the beginning of lecture quizzes are just vocab.

analysis.name: Thomas Nikolai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice, easy-going guy who you can tell really enjoys the content. No additional materials needed besides the posted lectures. My one warning is that the class isn't a slam-dunk 4.0 like the name would make you think, and the 3 unit tests + final (although they're open note) will sometimes touch on some of the more obscure points from lectures.

I took this along with World of Turf and I actually prefer this class over that one. The topics were interesting, the lectures were engaging and humorous (occasionally), and the professor actually cares for his students. Throughout the semester, he would give us so many updates/reminders. 4 total exams (final included) and 1 is dropped!

I recommend that everyone take this class! It's such a good class when you just need a few extra credits but don't want something difficult. Your grade is entirely based off of quizzes and tests but as long as you look over the lectures they are super easy. He makes the class very enjoyable and writes the nicest emails every week!

Honestly, an amazing professor. He's fully online and just has quizzes throughout the week that you have like a month to complete. I didn't even have to take the final because he only makes you keep 3 of the exams out of the 4. Also a really funny guy.
Insanely easy 4.0, he wants you to succeed.

analysis.name: Nicholas Ovenhouse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the best math professors I've had. His lectures are very clear and simple making them not hard to follow along. His office hours were the main reason I got A's on the tests so I highly recommend going to them if you ever need help on the content or just for review before a test. He is always very kind and helpful whenever you talk to him.

Calc 3 is one of the hardest classes I've taken at Michigan State, but the main difference I vastly prefer it over Calc 2 is because of Professor Ovenhouse. His lectures were always super detailed and he always went over good examples, which prepared you really well for homework and exams. 10/10.
He was good at explaining tough concepts. I didn't get the best grade because I missed some lectures towards the end but every time I attended I was able to understand the concepts, very nice guy.
He is really good and the class in really exam heavy but as long as you come to lecture and understand the material the class is light.

Nick is a great teacher. He obviously loves his subject and wants his students to do well. He's very organized and will answer any questions you have in a manner that benefits you as a student. He'll go over homework assignments to make sure you can complete them. The only downside is Lab Day - you'll have to work in groups on a large worksheet.

analysis.name: Rola Nashef

Professor Nashef is honestly one of my favorite professors at MSU. She genuinely cares about her students and their growth throughout the class, and she gives insightful lectures. Writing this review is the reason that I got an account on RMP. Professor Nashef is a very nice person who seems to really care about their students. The class is very fun too!

analysis.name: Nicole Geske

This class is nearly impossible if you don't spend every spare minute you have teaching yourself everything. I
Got to be one of the worst ways to teach a class.

One of the nicest professors I have had, very helpful and knowledgeable. Not a good teacher though, lectures are hard to sit through and lecture slides are 100+ slides long every day making it almost impossible to study them or use them for projects.

Bro she a GOAT. The course is chill, a lot of working but if you just see her videos and then go to lecture you'll be fine. She understands you got stuff going. analysis.name: Osvaldo Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

Such a nice professor!!! You also can tell how much he loves teaching this. Made class interesting enough for people who don't like science. Group projects that weren't awful although some days were more boring than others. Mandatory attendance but he usually lets us go early.

The TAs teach the course. I've never even met the main professor. If you get a good TA, then you will get a good grade. Luckily, mine was amazing!

In class assignments you can do from home, lectures are SO hard to sit through. three exams that were all taken online outside of class, not proctored. I would recommend to others for integrative studies requirement. very easy coursework that takes less than 10 mins. not a lot of homework at all

review_highlights.comment:
MC377: Culture, Politics, and Postcolonialism: Profiling Sub-Saharan Africa

I had Professor Elemo for MC 201 and am currently taking her MC 492 class. She does an excellent job explaining complex readings and breaking them down clearly. She is thoughtful, supportive, and genuinely cares about her students' success.

Professor Elemo's truly one of my favorite JMC professors. I had some medical issues towards the end of the semester and she was extremely understanding when it came to my absences (unlike some other professors). She's truly passionate about what she's teaching and talking to her about class material is extremely beneficial. Highly recommend!

I had her for MC 201. Though I didn't like her class my freshman year, I realized she's actually an amazing professor in MC325! She has amazing lectures, helpful during office hours, and overall a very understanding professor if you show up. Attendance is very important but you're allowed four absences which is much more than other professors.

Contrary to popular belief, she's a very good prof. Her tone may be condescending at times, but she teaches well and has clear expectations. She is a tough grader but provides good advice. Just take her feedback into account and go to office hours if you're struggling and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Orlando Hawkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My favorite JMC prof I've had thus far, he creates a comfy environment. I used to be so nervous to join discussions, but I was good to share my takes in this class. He gives genuine feedback, and will happily meet with you if you need help. He also lectures with slides instead of just yapping for a straight hour and a half. Pls take him he's great.

Professor Hawkins is a refreshing change in the PTCD lineup. He has moved away from the usual Straussian dogma toward a more critical, historically grounded approach. If you're a Straussian, you may not enjoy the critical readings so much, but there will be ample opportunity to interpret and grapple with the canonical texts. Participating is key!

Professor Hawkins is brand new to JMC/PTCD, but he is a truly great teacher. He really impressed me, and he did not shy away from tough topics, and fairly presented all the reasonable angles in this class, which is a pretty controversial class. I Highly, HIGHLY reccomend taking classes with him.

analysis.name: Oren Ziv

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst professors I've had. He relied way too heavily on his TAs to do everything, and it led to slow grades, assignments being assigned to the wrong dates constantly, and multiple other problems. His grading system is also horrible and convoluted. Definitely a mixed bag.

Seems like a good guy who teaches his class very harshly. Quizzes and tests are going to be hard, since there are 5–7 responses to choose from for each multiple-choice question and 3–5 responses for each T/F question. Nothing in this class is meant to help you achieve a good grade within reason, and that is wrong given the current student workload.

Awful class. For 98% of people it is a required class that is so obnoxiously hard. Relies too much on TAs so he is able to "focus more on content",he doesn't

analysis.name: Melissa Wurtzel O'shea

review_highlights.comment: i took pls120 and she was great! she's an attorney herself! attendance is mandatory!!! there's lots of reading + case briefs at first but you get used to them. 2 exams and a group project you have to ask and answer questions on. she lets you use notes on exams but they are handwritten so i had to rush a bit. highly recommend!

Attendance is mandatory but she typically lets us out a few minutes early so it makes up for it.

LOVED this class. At the start of the semester it was very daunting but once you understand the formula of how to write for her class you will be set. Very kind and knowledgeable professor, I will take another class with her in a heartbeat. This class is supposed to act as law school prep, so keep that in mind when considering taking 321.

This is an easy class, it is NOT a political science class. It is strictly law. She is a fair grader and its easy to pass the class. No one assignment will deck your grade. She is dramatic but it is an easy class to pass. You don't have to go to class but I would recommend it.

Professor O'Shea is a GREAT teacher, she makes law very fun and interesting even if it is only an intro class. There is ALOT of reading, there aren't any textbooks required for the course but for the first half of the semester you will have to read cases. Only two exams and a project, both open note. Easy A!!!

analysis.name: Matthew Pontifex

He was a decent professor, but I did think he had some egotistical tendencies.

Content is super interesting. Study it well and there's no reason this class will be too difficult. Pontifex has an ego and not everyone liked him, but I enjoyed his teaching style a lot. He is organized, straight-forward, and uses strategies during lecture to improve our chances of remembering the content (his examples given are always great)

Students should know that Professor Matthew Pontifex really cares about helping students understand the material. His lectures are engaging and he explains concepts clearly, which makes the class easy to follow. If you pay attention and participate, you will learn a lot. He is passionate about what he teaches and creates a positive environment.

I think that professor Pontifex is very knowledgable in what he teaches. In lecture, he makes specific examples that make the content easier to understand. There is extra credit given in specific lectures. I got a 4.0 without getting above an 88% of a test but I also never missed a lecture or lab. I recommend reading the lecture material!

He is pretty good with lecturing and knows what he's talking about but comes across kinda rude. I didn't find the content to be too bad but it's definitely test heavy and would recommend going to lectures to do well. Also has you do a check in for every class for points so those, the labs and the check for understanding quizzes are easy points

analysis.name: Riley Patzsch
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

Anatomy has lots of content, so he makes sure we all understand it by explaining it in simplistic ways and telling us what we really need to know for exams. Incredible guy.

Riley has been the best professor ive had at MSU. His office hours are sooooo helpful. The lectures can be pretty dense but he does verbally tell you what you should focus on for studying. He exapains things in the easiest and clearest way he can with it still making sense. Class is hard but he made it so much more managable. A++ for this man!

Professor Riley is definitely my favorite professor that I have had so far at MSU. He is extremely approachable, intriguing, down to earth, and relatable. He does a great job covering the material and making it clear what to know for the exams. You need to put in the time to study for this in order to be successful since it is mainly memorization.

AMAZING!!!! One of the best professors I've had at msu. He cares about making sure all of his students know and understand all of the information he is teaching. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does give random extra credit quizzes for those who attend lecture. I would love to take another one of his classes.

Riley is my favorite professor I have ever had at MSU. He is very approachable if you need to ask anything. Lectures are fast paced but he makes it interactive and lets you know exactly what you need to know for exams. Exams will be tough if you don't study, so put in the time and listen during lectures and it is an easy 4.0.

analysis.name: Che Peterson

Communication is amazing. He always give you ample time and notification when something is due. He is super easy to contact and understanding. One of the best professors I have had while completing my business minor.
Che is awesome! His class is very straightforward and all homework and exams are online with multiple attempts. If you can take the in person lecture you should!!

Took the online version, not a hard class. Lectures are monotone and read off slides. You'll need to buy the online textbook to do homework - $85. Also weekly discussion posts. analysis.name: Sarah Prior

I took SOC 316 but it wasn't an option. great professor! just make sure you read all the assigned readings, as you have to tie most of them to whatever assignment you are doing. there is no final exam, just final project.

This was my favorite class! Dr. Prior is an amazing professor, and I hope to take another class with her again. She cares about her students and is very knowledgable about her field. Lots of extra credit opportunities, and the lectures were incredibly interesting. Class is based off the textbook. Just pay attention and go to class, and you're good.

analysis.name: Paul Schauert

Great professor, very insightful and wise however he is a VERY tough grader on papers. Make sure you go to office hours and participate in class discussions, although you dont get marked for absences, it will seriously hurt you if you don't show up.

analysis.name: Aaron Madrigal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Madrigal is very intelligent and knows how to write very well. He gives you a very long time to do each project and is not too strict about due dates but do not take advantage of that. Sometimes he will say things that do not exactly make sense and use big words but as long as you write how he speaks and writes, you will be great.

The class is easy, but he talks in circles. The lectures are pointless, so you can just do homework for other classes. He is a huge pushover and will push back assignments if you ask. Overall, a very easy class, and a pretty respectable prof.

The class is two hours long and they are so boring. He rambles about nothing the whole class and then assigns a paper. He's a pretty easy grader and he's easy to talk to. He's really lenient, if you ask for an extended deadline, he'll give it to you. He checks attendance.

This prof is an easy 4.0. Even though he talks in circles sometimes and the lecture seems pointless sometimes, you have to go. You can just sit on your laptop all lecture, (got a lot of outside hw done). Initially every assignment is confusing, but he is good at explaining what he's looking for, so they're all super doable. Easy 4.0 & honors credit

Pros: Cool guy, very relaxed, and works with you whenever you need help and tell him. This man straight up does not teach, he just talks about random things during lectures. So easy. And I got no less than an 88 on all of my papers. Cons: He doesnt give feedback when grading, just good grades. Relies heavily on peer review. Such boring lectures.

analysis.name: Daniel Ahlquist
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: MC 111 with Professor Ahlquist is amazing! The class focuses on writing about conservation and the environment. His passion makes discussions engaging, and he values participation, so speak up! If you care about the topic, you'll love it. His feedback is thoughtful, pushing you to grow as a writer. Highly recommend for anyone interested!

Ahlquist is an amazing person and very, very nice professor. He is very into expanding native rights, and is generally against the use of technology to address social issues like climate change. if you disagree with him on both those, you should think twice. As someone who disagrees with him on those though, he is still a great professor

I'm so glad I took this class. It was my favorite in my first semester of JMC. He really did a lot of work to make his classroom a community and a safe space for all his students. Discussion matters, and participation matters, but the topics are so interesting that it was easy! Lots of reading, but it's mainly online articles. HAVE to read them.

I had him for MC111 this Fall semester. Super smart and caring, will help you throughout the course. It's a hard transition going into JMC, but he brightens the whole atmosphere. He creates a good environment where you can have fun, insert your opinion, ask questions, and learn. I highly recommend him for any course you choose to take.
I took MC111 with Ahlquist and definitely came away a better writer! He is very understanding when it comes to personal issues and is clear with his expectations for class.

analysis.name: Ron Southwick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED HAVING CLASS WITH THIS MAN!!! He literally made working out fun twice a week, SUCH a nice guy, I have no idea what all these ratings are, literally the kindest guy. There are 2 "practials" or "exams" where you have to show skills, but he will literally make you do it till you get it, and you will pass. Couldn't recommend enough.

He is very kind and supportive, always respecting the boundaries between student and teacher while still looking out for his students' well-being and safety. Joined the Taekwondo club just because his class was so much fun, and he created a very welcoming environment. I am still there to this day, even a year later!

Whoever is posting all these bad comments must be smoking something!  This is probably the most fun college classes I've taken.  Ron is a great professor and he treats everyone with respect.  He is aware of everyones abilities and he works with everyone on their own level.  Great class!

Ron is an excellant instructor, and overall nice guy.  He makes sure everyone understands, and is very considerate of people's different levels of physical ability.  I really enjoyed learning taekwondo with Ron, and will continue in the future.
Best class ever! Great professor!

analysis.name: Ehsan Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is insanely helpful and gives great feedback and you can definitely tell he wants you to succeed. It is a hard class for those French does not come easily to, so you'll have to put in effort. Manageable homework, short readings. Lots of quizzes/exams and a few papers. Participation is very important. You'll gain a great knowledge base in this.

This was my second time having Professor Ahmed and once again, I enjoyed him very much. Hes such a kind and generous professor with so much love for his students and his work. I really appreciate him and I hope to have more classes with him in the future. Hes an undeniable asset to the Department of Romance & Classical Studies.

Dr. Ahmed is a wonderful professor. He puts his heart and soul in his teaching and is extremely passionate about the French language. He also seems to be particularly interested in classic French literature. He is so kind, caring, flexibl. I wish that more college professors were like him. You're bery fortunate to have him.

analysis.name: Brian Ahmedani
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ahmedani is a great research methods instructor. This is generally a really hard course but he made it quite a bit easier. Now having said that, it's still alot of work. Just isnt as bad as it could be. Just be warned, DO NOT CHEAT. He is vigilant and will bust you (at least thats what he says).

Its an online course so you have to participate online. When not understanding the professor is easy to email and responds quickly. His lectures were good and the reading posted was a lot, but the course was easy to manage. The final exam was easy, I only used to DSM and the clinical cases books.

This guy is a great teacher, engaging, reasonable and empathetic.  Brian genuinely cares about the students and is sincere, but expects you to work.  He makes a difficult topic look easy.  I really may not have made it with a different professor.  Highly recommend!

This professor teaches a very difficult research methods class.  The class itself is a lot of work, but Prof. Ahmedani has a great deal of experience and shares this with the class, which livens things up.  He is very funny and jokes a lot.  He's often willing to help students.  He's also (easily) the hottest professor I've ever had in college.
He is not good at giving clear directions in class.  Read and follow the course syllabus--he treats it like a contract!

analysis.name: Sarah Ahrens
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was the perfect anatomy lab professor. Provided lots of visuals and hands-on specimens. Tried to make everything as clear as possible and genuinely wanted us to succeed. As long as you study her lectures and your notes, you will do great on the tests. Only problem was that there were only 2 tests so the grade weight on each was very high.

VERY hard subject. While it gets easier to comprehend the various topics and understand the terminology towards the end, there isn't often enough time to write everything down during the test that they are looking for. She can also be a little nit-picky on the tests when it's hard to understand what the question is asking for.

Awesome teacher! Funny and interesting--often supplements her powerpoints with videos and fun facts. Only teaches practical things you will need to know. Involves the class during her lectures with discussion and questions. A massive amount of info to learn in this class but she helps make it enjoyable and easier to remember.

analysis.name: Nwando Achebe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class covers a very wide range of African topics including religious and traditional history, modern culture and economic system but the tests are Blue Book essay tests that ask 3 or 4 very specific questions and leave a lot of the lecture material irrelevant since the tests are not cumulative. And recitation is mandatory with group presenting.

This class is really hard. There is a lot of writting and high expectations. The exams are brutal, long essays, and map quizzes. She is very nice, funny, and passinate about what she's teaching. But sometimes too passinate, like yells into her microphone until it hurts your ears.

Required gen ed but insanely hard. Wouldn't post lecture slides, recitations were brutal, assigned around 5 books, multiple midterms with 4–5 essay questions, plus random 30-second pop quizzes. Felt more like a grad seminar than a basic requirement. Way over the top and unnecessarily stressful.
Loved this Professor!! She seemed intimidating but when I went into her office hours she was completely down to earth and we ended up talking for two hours about non-class related things!!

Not a bad class, but definitely a lot of work. Lectures aren't mandatory, but there are 5 random pop quizzes in class throughout the semester, so you kind of have to go. TAKE GOOD NOTES, you'll need it when studying for midterm and final. Mandatory recitation on Friday's, so hopefully you get a good TA. I had Janelle Edwards who was fantastic.

analysis.name: Denise Acevedo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Talk about deranged. Denise had a political meltdown every other lecture. Always complaining about the administration has absolutely no respect for students who share other beliefs. Avoid her at all costs!

Dr. Acevedo was extremely kind and always willing to read your essays and gives amazing feedback on what you should add or take away from your essay. Class is mandatory but she understands if something comes up. I would 100% recommend taking WRA 101 with her especially if you like to mess around. Dr Acevedo likes to keep things fun and is genuine!!

Dr. Acevedo is kind and clearly cares about her students. The class is easy, with grades based only on four projects, including one group assignment. However, she often goes off on political rants and shares personal stories about past students that probably shouldn't be repeated. Different views don't feel welcomed or tolerated in her classroom.

This class wasn't well structured, and it wasn't all Acevedo's fault. She's very caring, kind, and energetic, but the class activities, assignments, and projects weren't the best in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory, but she's a flexible and caring professor.

Love her!! It's clear she loves her job and adores her students — very flexible and willing to work with you. Highly recommend, her class was very educational while maintaining a fun, relaxed atmosphere :). Takes student feedback into consideration and actually applies it to her curricula. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: Jeff Ackermann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: With little to no choice for an economics class, you will most likely get stuck with Ackermann. If this happens, I hope you are good at teaching yourself the entirety of microeconomics. Even with the video lectures, much is up to interpretation during the exams when you have to study eight different units for a single exam. Would not take again.

Honestly it's a whatever class, I can't claim bias or anything, but like I showed up, 3rd row to front, quiet, attentively. But its like every interaction is lol why do you like hate me. Like I just take it personal sometimes and couldn't help but feel like rip me. Like idk I think he's rude and bald sorry.

His class wasn't difficult per se. However, Professor Ackermann fought my RCPD coordinator on midterm extensions. I had life saving surgery, and only received a two-day extension for the first midterm. The work is definitely manageable, but his schedule is incredibly strict. Also, in-person exams for an online course are brutal. (EC 201 & 202)

DON'T TAKE MACRO FIRST! THIS WAS A MISTAKE! Ackermann always made the class fun and interesting, making me want to come to class every day. But man, he could NOT teach. He hardly goes over the content, often going on side tangents about family or the news. Be prepared to teach yourself and get yelled at if you email him if you're confused

not a lot of homework, you watch lecture videos then have a few assignments each week. 4 exams and one is dropped. chill class but it's hard because you basically teach yourself. I've heard he isn't easy to go to for help though I never did. just stay on top of everything since there isn't much to be graded on or turn your grade around.

analysis.name: Gautam Aishwarya
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So confusing and disorienting. Professor has messy writing and a very thick accent. Does not keep a cohesive schedule whatsoever. You walk in class, take notes, and take a test on the notes you took the class BEFORE. No time to study whatsoever.Even told me and my entire class we had a big exam the NIGHT BEFORE. 0 out of 1,000. Could not be worse.

Could not be more confusing. Horrible hand writing, extremely thick accent, constantly gives the wrong answer and then has to be corrected by students, super unclear communication. No real explanation ever, simply fills in the notes and then tests you on said notes the NEXT class. Don't take this class unless it is literally your only option.

I've never cried or called my mom for anything this much before this. I stopped going to lectures because I learned more from someone else teaching me than the professor. I was starting to think that I was the issue but I shouldn't have to pray that I get hit by a CATA bus on the way to my exams. If you're not religious, find one & start praying.

I've never hated my life more than when I took this class. I stopped going to lectures half way through semester because it was a waste of time since my math skills were actually regressing when he taught; Instead, I taught myself the topics through Youtube videos. I paid for this class yet I'm the one teaching. Don't take if you want to live.

His handwriting is extremely sloppy, students have ask what he wrote on the slide. Lectures are confusing, on top of his extremely thick accent. Very unorganized, answers questions incorrectly, and doesn't understand the questions students ask him. He often gives no help for the question that was asked by the student due to misunderstanding them.

analysis.name: Aklilu Zeleke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Course uses R-studio which is the coding portion. For exams, his coding portion will be taken at the same time frame. Other STT 231 professors allow you to take home the coding portion. He is super nice and gentle, but overall a boring professor. His lectures can be confusing due to the accent but he does offer some extra credit points.

DO NOT TAKE HIM! Actually so boring, horrible, hard to understand. In person R studio exam unlike every other STT 231 professor. I've heard take Horr, from everything I hear the class is nothing like Zeleke's was. He was really sweet just shouldn't be teaching.

Dr. Zeleke is a super caring professor who will do what he can to help you succeed. Although attendance isn't mandatory, it's vital to attend lectures as he works on a chalkboard & doesn't post his notes/lectures online. He offers lots of practice problems & extra credit, & his exams are fairly similar to the practice offered. I highly recommend!

Dr. Zeleke is an incredibly kind and enthusiastic professor. However, in my opinion he is not the best teacher and studying for exams can be increasingly difficult and stressful. There is lots of homework too. There are many opportunities for extra credit too. My advice: Go to every class you can, do the homework, and go to office hours.

I enjoyed this class especially trying to refine my statistics skills. I took a stats class in the summer at OCC and I found that some stuff was the same, but the formulas were slightly different. In this class, I would personally say that I struggled with the R-studio part because I would always get error message when I was typing in command.

analysis.name: Jeff Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved learning about economics in high school. Unfortunately, this professor has now ruined the subject for me. He somehow found a way to make it a mundane, boring chore. It is extremely lecture-heavy, and I felt he explained things in an unnecessarily complicated manner. Ackerman is extremely inaccessible as well.

Professor Ackermann successfully (jokingly) catfished me into becoming an economics major. He actually made economics interesting and fun to learn, which in turn made me think the department was all like that. Boy was I wrong, almost every other Econ professor outside of him is monotone, boring, and old. I enjoyed Econ when I had him, now I don't.

Literally the funniest prof ever. Such an amazing guy and you can really tell that he cares abt the class and has passion for what he does. I was undecided before coming to college but after taking his class, made me want to pursue an econ degree. Funny lectures, 3 midterms and 1 final exam but only 3 exam grades count, really helpful study guides.

I would say that this class is pretty doable as a freshman. He gives a lot of resources and I believe that the homework assignments (both completion and accuracy) and especially the study guides both give a lot of information to help when it comes to exams. This class demands a lot of effort though so make sure you're staying on track.

Very nice and funny guy. Really like his teaching and personality. In his class however, he didn't allow calculators or cheat sheets like every other professor. His 3.5 was also 4.0 in other classes. Despite him being a very good teacher, I'd rather have easier access to a 4. Recommendation is to choose a different one. Attendance is manditory.

analysis.name: Akil Cornelius
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Cornelius is fun, but his class is very hard. If you see him teaching this class and Jack the Ripper & Victorian England, this class is not about that. This class is on African Traditional Religion and Warfare & the final is 40% of your grade. The concepts are very abstract and hard to grasp. Fun teacher, but try your luck elsewhere

Don't go near him if you're gonna take this course. Daily 30-50 pg readings that will be on the final. Pop quizzes with a 10 min time limit. Doesnt let you see your grade until you have taken the final, meaning you have to email him to see your grade. Lectures are only pictures, so notes are based on what he's saying or notes on the readings.

He is a genius and very passionate about what he teaches. Not a tough grader, but you're going to have to do some research and reading. The material is pretty interesting so it's not too bad. One of my favorite professors.

Prof is very passionate, but grade is entirely based on weekly essays, participation, and a 8-10 page final that is 40% of your grade. If you miss lecture you miss all of the material, but all the essays are based on the 30+ page articles you have to read 2x a week. Class is very interesting, but very stressful and difficult.

Mr. Cornelius was the absolute BEST TA I have ever had. He is very inspirational, energetic, and cares about all of his students. I can not recommend any class/section with him enough. You will not regret it at all.

analysis.name: Shastri Akella
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a nice and amazing person. He really cares bout his students and fosters and kind and nurturing environment. As long as you show up, participate, and do the work, you will have a wonderful time and grow so much as a writer.

He's really sweet! His grading for his Creative Fiction Writing class is just making sure you complete assignments on time, and making sure you participate in class. The class's workload is probably 3/5, so not too much or too little. He's also an enthusiastic professor, and willing to work with you to meet your needs.

Shastri is so sweet. Big fan of him. Intro to Creative Writing was very much that, an introduction where you explore different forms of creative writing. His grading scale is pretty clear and as long as you actively participate and give feedback during class, you should be fine. Feedback has a focus on positive aspects as it is an intro class.

analysis.name: Akin Òsénì
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Literally an awful professor. Never knew the answers to any question I asked. The assignments were so confusing because he never explained them. He also didn't know how to work the online D2L system. 0/10 DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES.
He was very bad and didn't know how to use D2L to put assignments in. Never responds to emails and doesn't have office hours. Good luck if you get stuck with him.
Doesn't know how to work D2L. Won't email you back at all. Sucks at communicating about literally anything.

analysis.name: Akiko Imamura
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: ASIANLAN426 (Advanced Spoken Japanese), Imamura is the only teacher of the class and it is organized very poorly. The homework has an insane amount of typos and when it comes to preparing speeches, there are no examples and explanations are not clear. Her "feedback" is extremely blunt and rude, and sometimes just downright hurtful.

Imamura Sensei was a great professor, definitely recommend taking her class! She rly cares abt her students. You have hw and class every day, so make sure that your other classes aren't too time-consuming- languages requires consistency and time. However, it was such a rewarding & fun class, I also loved getting to know my classmates.

She does give a lot of homework, but that's expected of a class with a language as difficult as Japanese. If you do have mistakes, she will ask you to resubmit a new corrected version of the assignment, but it's all for your own benefit. She's a great teacher and everyone in the class really seemed to enjoy having her as a teacher.

Overall great teacher that does everything you can ask for from a uni level language professor. Very clear with her expectation and grading, takes her time and fully explains everything very well. Clear deadlines, goals, and instructions the entire course. 100% would recommend

Imamura sensei is a wonderful teacher! She really cares about how you're doing in class and helps you as much as she can. Even though the class is a lot of work, if you're able to attend everyday and keep up with the content, it will be pretty easy.

analysis.name: Donald Akanga
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is super sweet and checks in with us to make sure we are all okay and to remind us of due dates in our GroupMe. There are about four papers that we had to do (not very long), and there is about 20 pages of reading per week with a weekly quiz. Overall, a great professor who cares about his students and the information at hand.

GEO221 online. He was great! Very responsive outside of class (online course) via email, and the labs were very easy to follow. Some may say there's a lot of labs/assignments (I personally didn't think so), but there's no exams, and as long as you set a decent amount of time between beginning the assignment and the deadline, you'll be alright.
His class is a lot of work, but he makes the instructions very clear and you will receive a good grade as long as you follow them. Not a difficult grader.
Inaccessible in terms of help and assigns loads of assignments.

analysis.name: Ramin Akbari
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: literally the worst teacher I've ever had. the dude has existential crises in class and doesn't teach anything helpful, and didn't even know when our midterm was. there's maybe two people in the class that actually know what's going on. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM.
Would give a 0 if possible. Avoid this TA if you can help it.
Honor section is more difficult compared to other sections.
You have to study lectures before class. Useful material.

analysis.name: Jameel Al-Haddad
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a very nice guy and is willing to help, but the class feels like a waste of time, its reaching the end of the semester and he still hasn't graded past the first notebook. His lectures and instructions are also pretty confusing at times overall would avoid this class if it is not required.

His criteria contradict themselves all the time, so it's hard to get a good grade because it's hard to understand what needs to be done. The class feels like a mess, and it's tough to understand the work that needs to be done. He will help you out a great deal and is very nice to talk to. Just not the best instructor.

Please for the love of God and your sanity do not take this class. It's only week 4 and it makes me want to die. Its unorganized, poorly structured, too much going on, and classes are overwhelming and vague. Please just don't take this class.

This man takes absolutely forever to grade anything-- even if it is just releasing scores from a multiple choice D2L quiz. He is also very nit-picky when grading. Most of the material must be learned before the lectures, because he is going to go on ten tangents and cover maybe 25% of the material in class. If you have to take him, best of luck.

The lectures were pre-recorded videos to be watched outside of class where Jameel read off of a powerpoint. The lectures took a few hours even on 2X speed when I took notes. There were pre-class quizzes and weekly post-class quizzes as well. Jameel is a nice person but is not great at explaining lecture content for a 2-hour long class.

analysis.name: Alexandra Allweiss
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Alex was an amazing instructor who clearly cared about her students and the material she taught. She kept the class engaged and knew how to pull us back in when attention drifted. The freedom she gave us in assignments was deeply appreciated by my peers and me. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, take it.

Alex was a great professor, and I really enjoyed her class. She was so caring and respectful of everyone in class and what they thought. She was very understanding about late work and gave great feedback. All the content assigned felt necessary and meaningful to the course. Participation and group work were highly encouraged in every class session.

I took Alex's TE 353 class, and she was awesome! Super interesting lectures and in-depth discussions. She clearly is very knowledgable and passionate about our material and is so caring for us and our needs. Classes were dynamic and so fun to attend every time, plus she brought food every week. I loved this class and would love to have Alex again!!
Alex cares very much what her students think. She works hard to make sure everyone understands the homework, but she also expects you to bring your perspective into the discussion.

The contents we learned about are very interesting, and even though I don't like reading, the articles and books assigned are some of the best. Alex was very considerate of us and was always making sure to give us extra credit options and grade in a timely matter. Along with that, she's just funny and loving; definitely my favorite prof so far!

analysis.name: Erik Altmann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Erik is a kind professor, but I would not recommend him overall. Each class is a lecture with a PowerPoint. Exams are pretty much the entirety of the grade. Exams are difficult, and often 2 answers are correct (and he admits this too). You will only have lectures to study for exams. He is a funny dude, though.

Nice guy, but VERY BORING. Lecture should not be 2 hours long for a 15 slide powerpoint. Maybe its because I am an upperclassman in a lower level 100 course, but damn I was not paying attention at all because he's just that boring. Very open to questions and clearly passionate but probably not built to be a professor.
Genuinely thought I was gonna fail this class even though I took AP psych in highschool and have gotten 4.0's in all classes since coming to MSU.

Incredibly test heavy which makes it difficult to ace. No practice exams, homework assignments, or study guides to gauge your knowledge so you are going into every exam blind. There are also no extra credit or corrections which is understandable, but if you want to have any kind of confidence going into these exams this course isn't it.

This class is wickedly uninteresting. The professors tone, slides, and presentation style will have you asleep. This class relies solely on exams for grading which does not account for different learning styles. This class is a complete waste of time and I am losing precious hours of my life by attending. Avoid this prof if possible.

analysis.name: Alexander Johnson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Previous reviews on this class scared me. While this class was somewhat hard, the prof truly cares about his students succeeding, & lectures are very interesting. You will need to genuinely study for his exams in advance and 10% of the questions are based on niche things he mentions once, the rest is straightforward imo as long as you study well.

Required lecture attendance, graded TopHat (accuracy), and some homework assignments. 4 midterms and the final, lowest score is dropped, so you could skip final. The instructor sometimes explains concepts in a confusing way and occasionally goes off on tangents, but he is very kind and always willing to answer questions. I wouldn't buy textbook.

Dr. Johnson's lectures were definitely interesting. He does talk fast, but he answers any questions and clarifies anything that his students need. He drops one exam, and if you study the powerpoints and go to class you should do well on them. Overall a good professor.

I struggled a little with some of the concepts in the class and had to study for this more than I was used to. The lectures are information heavy but he is a good teacher and you definitely want to come to class otherwise you're screwed. Drops lowest exam so you can skip the final and gives extra credit if needed based on test scores.

This has been one of my most challenging classes thus far. However, I would like to emphasize that Prof Johnson is a really fantastic guy and professor. His exams are incredibly difficult, but he has given us extra opportunities to boost our grades if we are struggling. This class is fascinating and I recommend it if you're up for a challenge!

analysis.name: Allison Dellapelle

analysis.name: Stephen Arch

There's a lot of reading, but the books are very interesting.

I really enjoyed his poetry class, I learned a lot about poetry. Class was built around reading and in-class discussions, with some on-demand writing/annotation exams. I would definitely recommend him as a professor, he clearly knows what he's talking about and is easy to listen to.

Great guy! I took his Gothic course back in freshman year, and it was excellent. Definitely some work, but he's an enjoyable professor who really cares. Sadly, I think he stopped teaching the Gothic IAH course, but he's still a very good and passionate professor. The work and readings can be a lot, but it's manageable.

analysis.name: Kirk Astle

Professor Astle is an easy grader and likes participation. As long as you complete assignments, you will get a great grade in the class. A lot of busy work, but honestly, it just helps your overall grade in the end. I would 100% take a course with Professor Astle again.

99% of the class is writing a million mini essays on one topic, which i dont hate at all. the assignments themselves were relatively easy but this dude talks for a very long time while saying so much nothing. 7/10 since class ends early most days

analysis.name: Zarena Aslami

Aslami is great. I had her for ENG 280 in the spring of 2023, as well as this last semester for ENG364. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

analysis.name: Ashley Moore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

Dr. Moore is an incredible professor.  She is open about every decision made in the class. After the Feb. 13 event, she was helpful and reached out with support and resources. Ashley was one of the most caring professors I have had to date. She is very understanding and always wants you to take care of yourself before school. She is a professor who truly cares about each of her students and their well-being. She is respectful of everyone in the classroom when discussing important topics. She is so real with her students and this helps with her teaching which she is very well organized and prepared for. I would highly recommend taking a class with her.

analysis.name: Ashley Triplett

Reading straight off of the powerpoint slides does not constitute teaching, and it didn't really seem like she wanted to be there. I am disappointed with how the class turned out, and it could be structured a whole lot better.

Horrible lectures. Reads straight from PowerPoint with little to no added substance. There was no additional homework when I took the class, so you just had to pray you did well on the 5 major exams. Stress.

Dr. Triplett understands that her class is hard, and she is always willing to help outside of class. Granted, the lectures are not super interesting, but it's a fair trade because the all the homework can only help your grade (so long as you actually complete it). You'll have to study hard-- exams are difficult. But she offers tons of extra credit.

analysis.name: Asa Brigandi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

The class was an easy A, but class attendance is a portion of the grade. You have to buy the textbook to get online homework access, but you can go over the homework in office hours and get 100%. Really receptive to questions. Review lectures and study materials really helped with exams.

analysis.name: Arthur Athanason

Love her! She's amazing and really goes out of her way to help students.

she will not respond to emails but she is a nice lady and cares about your success she does take a while to grade things and did not give feedback when points were marked off going to class was only important when it involved assignments (index cards)or projects, besides that it was pointless it was a okay class but i would not take it again

analysis.name: Avery St. Dizier

Ayman is amazing, 11/10 prof. He is super understanding that the language is hard and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also did a really good job of proctoring an online class in a way that felt personal. Homework is necessary for learning the material but it's not overly difficult!!

SWEETEST MAN ALIVE!! He is so cute (such a dad) and teaches Arabic so well. He grades pretty leniently because he knows how tough the language is but he also makes sure we learn our stuff. He's very quiet (kind of mysterious) and doesn't talk much but I would take a bullet for this man.

Lots of homework in the beginning but drops off @ end. Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at MSU and I wish I could take more courses with him. Very funny and caring guy!

Amazing Professor. She is super kind and down to earth. All you need to do is show up and participate in the discussion and you'll do just fine! Probably the best TA I have had so far.
Honestly the best TA I have ever had. She made going to class worth it and I enjoyed every lecture. Professor A puts effort into being engaging and she is very funny.
Professor Ismail was amazing!! I would recommend her to anyone in the university. She was constantly kind and funny. 100% would take again.

analysis.name: Aylin Alin

Dr. Azadnia is great! analysis.name: Cara Schwarz

Lectures were very clear and helped me understand the concepts. Plenty of practice in D2L and quick to respond on Piazza or Email. While the class is exam-heavy, they didn't have any trick or tedious questions. I would take this professor if you are in BioChem or are taking the MCAT at some point bc she goes over a lot of biological applications.

The professor was nice and recorded all the lectures online. However the class was taught poorly and the lectures were often confusing, I had to do a lot of teaching myself outside of class. The recitations were even more confusing, as well as the homework. There were only a few extra credit assignments that barely helped my grade.

analysis.name: Caroline Szczepanski

Horrible teacher overall. Lectures are completely useless and don't help you learn at all yet are required. You learn everything from the textbook. A ton of reading assignments but the weekly hw isn't the worst. Impossible for her to stay consistent with her own key. Worst grading I've ever seen. Doesn't like people who don't participate in class.

Need an 85 to get a 4.0, not as easy as it sounds. Liu's lectures are tough to follow, and I basically had to teach the entire class to myself. Exams are worth about 70% of your total but exam class averages were around a 65% and there was no curve. If you have minimal experience in econ prior to this course I would consider a different professor.

Ce Liu wouldn't be a recommendable professor if economics comes harder for you. On exams, I got a 75% when I played Papa's Pizzeria in class, compared to when I actually listened and studied, I got a significantly lower score. His lectures are very confusing as he spends too much time on the easy questions and too little time on the harder ones.

This was one of the worst classes ive taken. The 85 for a 4.0 is NOT easy. I attended every lecture, took notes, studied, did all homework, and still got below 68 on each exam. Cheat sheet seems like it'll help but since theres only 32 questions on 5+ chapters its hard to know what to put on there, I barely ended up using them. Would NOT recommend

i loved her she was so sweet. I went to every class and rarely had to do anything outside of class. i had a 8am but it was worth it to me

Genuinely sweet human and great professor. Gives a lot of time for the work to be done and has extremely clear requirements. She knew every student by name and seems to actually care for them. Very easy class with a very good professor if you even put in like 60% effort you should have no struggle getting a 4.0 this class. Highly recommend

Dr. C is one of the most caring professors I have met at MSU, she is truly interested in your journey as a writer and wants you to enjoy class and learning in general. Also very open to assisting with honors options, or any projects that are of interest to you.

My favorite professor ever, never meant a teacher who cared more about her students. Always would help and wants her students to get a 4.0. If you do the work you will 4.0. Do anything in your favor to get her!

analysis.name: Jill Chrobak
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chrobak is so sweet and helpful. Her class is honestly very easy, and she keeps everything very organized in D2L. She is accessible outside of class if you have any questions. A lot of the times she lets you out of lecture early which is really nice.

I had her for a hybrid WRA 101 course. I was worried initially but it was really nice. We got out of class early most (every) day and while there were occasional readings and assignments to do outside of class, they didn't feel like busywork. A lot of the smaller weekly assignments directly related to the large assignments. Definitely recommend.

Incredible professor. Very easy going and makes writing assignments enjoyable. No exams and gives helpful feedback for each writing assignment. I would definitely recommend taking her class if you need an easy writing class to take. Given 3 excused absences.

Amazing prof! Super well organized with her schedule and resources. I would recommend her to any student! I definitely grew as a person from the projects in her class, she was very intentional with what she assigned which was so helpful. She really does have everyone's best interest in mind. An easy and enjoyable 4.0!

Professor Chrobak is an awesome and nice but you need a 95% in the class to get a 4.0. She will only round if you have a 94.5% or higher. I recommend taking her class just make sure you double check the rubric and your papers are error free.

analysis.name: Christopher  Emery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I totally recommend him! Super fun and laid back. He is so passionate about what he teaches and it shows! He's also accommodating and he genuinely really cares about his students. He always has a smile on his face and he loves to see students' work. He does a lot of group projects, so if you're not into that thing, that's something to be aware of.

Professor Emery is really nice and wants his students to acheive. His class consists of lectures, and the midterm and final are group projects, which is nice. Most of the homework you receive is weekly discussion posts about topics you learned in class that week. I would recommend only buying the least expensive book he tells you to purchase.

Professor Emery is kind, and it's clear that he truly loves teaching. For this IAH course, we watched & analyzed horror movies, which I absolutely loved. We watched a lot of really good stuff, and the discussions were also engaging. There was little homework, usually just a discussion post a week, 1 group presentation, a final project, & a midterm.

Prof Emery is so nice and understanding. His lectures are never too intense and he often has breaks. We also get out early more often than not. There are no quizzes/exams, just a midterm group project and final group project plus one discussion post a week. You get 4 absences, your grade goes down by .5 (letter grade) per absence after. Nice class

Professor Emery is a great prof. The work load of this class can be a lot, but nothing one couldn't handle. We watch horror films in class and analyze them in class discussion, as well as for the hw discussion posts. Other than that we have group presentation and group final. Overall, very understanding and kind professor.

analysis.name: Christina  Myers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is a typical 100-level communications course. The content frequently reflects strong political viewpoints that are always overly emphasized, and the grading standards were unexpectedly rigorous given the limited depth and substance of the material.

Don't take this class unless you have to. Ta's grade strict, professor expresses politics, lots and lots of busy work, pointless assignments, and you have to cite literally everything you do, even if they give it to you. Wish I didn't take it!

Omg I loved her. Had her for the honors section and she was very inspirational to listen to and was very accessible by email. A lot of writing and research out of class, which as a non-JRN major, I thought was super interesting. Overall, she is awesome and the TA's graded very easily!

Awesome professor who is passionate about not only the subject matter but about hearing from and supporting the students themselves. I learned a lot about journalism from this class. Workload is manageable, sometimes there are big assignments but nothing too much.

class is easy work wise but the TA's are so hard on grading and will not anwser your email when you try to reach out to them for any reason. It depends on which TA you have but I wouldn't take this class if your not really strong with writing.

analysis.name: Samantha Cass
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't get me wrong, Cass is not a bad professor at all. She has years of experience in chemistry, however exams can be something else. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry in high school , I would try to take CEM 141/142, which is the natsci sequence. Taking LB chem it is implied that you have a very good understanding of chemistry from high school.

The method of teaching was a lot of doing all the learning outside of class then coming to class to do practice. Her method of teaching just did not click with me as a student who needs in-depth explanations for difficult topics. Not a super hard class but if you want in-depth explanations I would recommend trying a different professor.

Exam heavy, lectures are mandatory. Some of the exams were super tough and included material that was briefly covered. There are far easier professors in the Briggs program that offer tons of extra credit and aren't nearly as exam heavy. If you aren't a good test taker don't take this course!

I had her class when jamboard was used. Course was flip model, so we worked on materials during class and learned the stuff at home. It was lots of team involvement so pray you have a good team. Most of her exams was very hard since she was picky with the answers. She is seriously one of the harder prof for first years taking intro to chem.

I had Dr. Cass for both chem 2 and my senior seminar, and she is such a warm and caring professor. Her grading criteria is very clear and she is willing to make exceptions when necessary. She encourages thoughtful conversation and engagement with course content and going to her class was always pleasant.

PR 300, very caring and wants to set up her students for a successful career!

analysis.name: Cindy Hunter Morgan

Cindy Hunter-Morgan is an absolutely amazing professor. I cannot stress enough how inspirational her passion for writing is, or how much she cares about her students. She helped me improve my writing tremendously over the course of the semester, and even as an "English person" her class challenged me to become a better writer. tldr; she's awesome!

Cindy Hunter Morgan is the best human that I have met at this university. She has inspired me to WANT to read and write in my free time. She makes you work for the grade but I know that she just sees everyone's potential. I just wanna give her a hug.

analysis.name: Cimberly Weir

Attendance is MANDATORY. If you don't show up you won't pass. Group project is a huge part of the class with multiple presentations. She gets mad at students for having their computers open or doing anything besides paying attention. She will also get mad at you for being 5 mins late.

Cimberly is a very nice professor. But I felt like she would send condescending emails to you if you hadn't submitted a discussion, even if it was before the due date. In office hours, she would be very distracted and not really listening to you. I get she's busy but the multitasking made me feel unimportant.

Overall, the class is an easy 4.0. If you go to class and complete your assignments it's a guaranteed A. The problem I had with her is that she can be very condescending whenever you speak to her, as many have said before. She gets worked up when the class isn't engaged, but gives lackluster lectures that sways no student to be engaged.
Super easy class but she is a micromanager in every way

I know theory is important but she's so incredibly boring

Professor Cifaldi is great! She's really kind and you definitely won't have a bad time in her class. She genuinely cares for what she teaches and her students wellbeing. Super understanding. Dr. Cibelli is so smart, kind, and passionate and so clearly wants his students to succeed. His exams are majorly based on the quizzes and in class questions. 10/10 recommend.
He really cares about what he teaches and is very knowledgeable about reproduction! Cares about his students.

The material itself was pretty confusing and he goes through the lectures super fast but as long as you write everything down from his slides you'll be good. All his quizzes and exams were online and most of the material could be found on his lecture slides.

This prof was AWESOME!! Super helpful and knowledgable about animal reproduction. Everything that was on exams/ quizzes could be directly found in the powerpoint slides, so I'd recommend writing everything down. He kept things interesting and genuinely cares for his students.

Bruh this teacher honestly doesn't know what she's talking about

analysis.name: Ryan Claytor

review_highlights.comment: This professor will mark you late for being a minute off time a class period after he was five minutes tardy himself. STA201: Loved this class. LOTS of work depending on how ambitious you are. Show up to class even if you don't have the project done. Chime in during discussions. It's always been a dream of mine to make comics and this class has let me do that. 
Btw you don't need the course pack if you're a digital artist. Ames lettering at most for one assignment

Honestly, it's the participation. As another rating said, if you are even 30 seconds late he will mark you absent. I was 1 minute late once, and I walked in and he had already started lecturing. He doesn't even wait for class to start to take role. The class is also focused heavily on time-management, but it's HIS time management. Not good for all.

He obviously knows what he's talking about, but does so in a way that is accessible and down-to-earth. If you're interested in exploring the comics medium or diving in to improve your work, the comics courses with Ryan Claytor are a great way to go. Workload is a bit demanding, but I've never experienced another class that made me feel so proud!

analysis.name: Claire Vallotton

Don't take if you can avoid. I get it's a parenting by class but it's all from her parenting perspective and I feel like very few lectures helped on the THREE 6 page papers. EXTREMELY tough grader

HDFS 414.... 3 papers- very detailed and had to use scientific evidence. I wouldn't take her again but it was fine. Some discussions in class. Papers were kinda hard and they SUCKED. Don't think it is just an easy A. Hard grader on essays
