Most of the work needs to be done on the weekends and they are graded harshly. You never know what to expect in class and be prepared to not have enough time to do anything!

analysis.name: Melanie Cooper
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cooper was rude the entire semester and belittles the class for not understanding material that she can't teach correctly. She doesn't write on slides so if you're rewatching lectures, you will be lost. Alex (hw site) was painful to get through and is worth 10%. Recitation helped for understanding content. You can find Textbook pdf online

Dr. Cooper is a caring and honest professor. She might be a bit blunt for some people but I think she's hilarious, She definitely does care about her students' learning too

Actually pay attention and take notes in lecture, take the 45 minutes to actually do BeSocratic activities, check your notes a few times a week and no reason to not get a 4.0

Professor Cooper made the class way harder than it should've been. She states the facts but doesn't teach the reasoning behind them. The tests weren't difficult because of the material, but because they were confusing and worded badly. Homework is assigned after every class but doesn't take very long. I'd recommend choosing any other professor.

This class was hard. I ended somehow with a 2.5 but had a 1.5 for most of the class. Never got above a 50% for the first 2 texts. Textbook is a waste it doesnt help. Homework is due before every class. There is iclicker for attendance but you can drop 2 and its not for accuracy. some people get this chem and some dont. I had many tears here

Chemistry is always hard, however i truly love her. watching lecture videos immediately after class is a LIFESAVER. She is so funny, and makes the class more enjoyable. she responds to emails very quickly, and truly wants the best for her students. If you are taking this class, you will do fine if you truly apply the work and take the extra time.

analysis.name: Henry Cowan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You can do fine on quizzes if you go to every lecture. Lecture slides are posted after class. I averaged a 98% on quizzes by going through the slides and typing everything up and reviewing it. Lectures are interesting. EC is available through SONA, or an essay. Very interesting topics discussed in class, and you can tell Prof Cowan is passionate.

I honestly liked him as a professor; he was very professional. But it's not open note now for quizzes and exams. I do very poorly on quizzes if I miss class, SO i really recommend going and taking notes from what he's talking about. Tip: definitely don't remember the material, and even less so how to apply it to the quizzes and exams.

Mr. Cowan was very professional and talked a lot during class. He said his exams were hard—and they were. Even though they were only 20 questions and open-note, I felt stressed due to limited time and space. I wish there were more interactive activities. Homework was light—just one weekly Achieve task.

He wants us to be challenged a little bit and writes the quizzes in a way that we would be stimulated. I loved the material and didn't mind it, and this was easily my favorite class this semester! The material is pretty clear. although it goes a little fast.

Prof. Cowan is a great guy and very professional. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I found that I would perform poorly on quizzes if I missed class. There are four quizzes with one drop, but even though they are open note, I got mediocre scores. Little to no homework, but make sure you study hard for the quizzes (they make up 40% of your grade).

analysis.name: Corrine Higley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's nice and approachable. In each class, you answer mandatory ICA questions from the slides with your table group as she lectures. Iclicker attendance. Group CER's. Practice exams are usually identical to the real ones, so fill your note sheet to the brim. The repettiveness can become boring, but bear through it, there's few absences allowed.

BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD. She's extremely passionate about biology and it shines in her lectures. She's well rounded and cares about her students plus she's funny and adds memes to her slides! Whats not to love??? The exams are very similar to the practice exams and as long as you participate in class + complete ICA's, you are bound to succeed.

Grading criteria and concepts are relatively simple. Her lectures are good and she makes the materials simple to understand (no curve ball questions on exams). Exams are relatively straightforward and practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams. The assignments are collaborative. Only issue I have is that you need a 92% to get a 4.0

Overall good professor. Her lectures were engaging and she tried to make the class fun. The work was mildly difficult but she made it easier to understand. Not too sure about other BS162 professors, but she would be a good option if you need to take BS162.

Your lab group definitely makes a difference, and I was lucky mine worked well together. The professor was extremely nice and passionate, and she would give extensions if you needed and emailed her. Doing things with R was a little difficult, but she works through it with you. Going out to collect samples was SO fun too, I had a blast.

analysis.name: Marcie Cowley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She cancels class at least once a week with less than an hour warning. Did not seem interested in helping each student. Just read off slides word for word. Tests are online and open note. Only 3 attendance drops and she takes attendance twice per class.
She was at most okay; she would cancel class less than an hour before it started (she did it at least once a week). There is a lot of group work  and a lot of reading but it is easy

She's definitely a talker and will not stop, but she is nice. The class is very easy, but it is two hours long and feels repetitive. You have to do two hours of community service every week. I liked the volunteering part, but going to class was boring. There is group work every class, attendance is mandatory, and most of your grade depends on it.

The class is really easy. When I took it, the class was only about European migration with a focus on the 2015 European migrant crisis. The class is interesting if you enjoy social studies. Exams are online, and you don't have to be in the class to take them. Every class, you will have attendance and a quiz of one question relating to the material.

This class was easy, just show up to class, but beware of the attendance and the in-class quiz, which opens up just for 1 minute. The exam is open-book and online. She is super friendly and has group workshops, which are not the hardest. Honestly, easy credit for class and would recommend.

analysis.name: Sean Couch
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easily one of my favorite professors I've had during my time at the university. He makes learning engaging in his lectures, but definitely be prepared to write notes from what he's saying since the slides are mostly just visuals (equations/photos). The homework can take a while, too, with some Python code in there. The quizzes/exams aren't hard!

The professor himself is actually really good. He's extremely funny and you can tell he's passionate about this field. He enjoys teaching it. My only complaint is with his GOD AWFUL TA's. Their egos are high and their grading criteria is higher. They are rude and not helpful in their emails. This course would be miles better without Levi Webb.

I love Prof. Couch. His lectures are so interesting and he makes them very engaging. If you genuinely pay attention in class and do a majority of the homework, you will not need to do much else to prepare for the quizzes/final. He gives points for attendance, and he drops 2/6 of the quizzes. The key to get a 4.0 is genuinely just to go to class.

The professor was a really cool guy and you could tell that he enjoyed what he taught. The problem was the material. For a beginner level astronomy class for non-stem majors it was really difficult. A lot of textbook reading and multiple choice homework but also a lot of extra credit was offered.

He doesn't teach its all through the book. He overloads us with information in class that is not relevant to the quizzes. He's just there to flex what he knows when this is a beginner class. Only 6 quizzes in the gradebook so if you do poor on those good luck!!

analysis.name: Cristina Schmitt
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take this class in the spring. The lectures are atrocious and incredibly difficult to follow. She is very disorganized and cant answer a question without creating 3 more. Often shows she is confused about content. Shes a nice lady with good intention but not a good instructor. TAs grade harsh, ive had questions wrong that I did with the professor.

Be ready to become a linguistics master(on your own time)Lectures and textbook were usually unhelpful, you HAVE to go to office hours/help room + be cautious of due dates bc they are easy to miss. The exams weren't horrible, and I managed to get an A after studying a TONNNN. You will cry over this class. Try to do homework early so you can get help

She is very disorganized and not the best at explain the content of the class. Her lectures are also not structured, making them hard to follow and understand. However, she did offer a lot of extra credit on the final (added up to 20% to midterm exam grade). Her intentions are there but her lack of organization makes the class difficult.

I will NEVER take this class with her again. Try to take this class in the spring with a different professor if you can. Lectures were unorganized and I lost points on the homework for problems she helped with. Make sure to go to the TAs instead (they grade them). D2L course was also never updated with lecture material, so you have to go to class.

The professor is a great person, BUT she was extremely disorganized. You have to go to class and take notes since nothing is posted online. If you miss class, then you will most definitely be behind. The overall grade in the class is determined only by harshly graded weekly homework assignments and 2 exams. Take this class with another professor!

analysis.name: Rene Crespin

review_highlights.comment: It isn't said anywhere, but you should definitely take EC420 before this class. So far it is very regression heavy. The slides are the worst part of the class. Poorly made, spelling and grammar errors everywhere. Midterm is coming up and it is so hard to study if you want to read the slides. To be fair, the subject is pretty interesting.

Class structure is well taught. Majority of the material is being able to read and interpret graphs, basic econometrics but not rigorous whatsoever. Professor is willing to meet if you are having issues, attendance is not worth much. Don't let the other reviews deter you this class is a much better option than other ec 400 classes.
Lectures are easy to understand, homework is pretty easy, takes attendance regularly.

Knows plenty about education economics but not how to teach. Would read off poorly made slides that he refused to even post on D2L which makes it incredibly hard to study. Had no clear learning goals or objectives for each unit so I didn't know what to learn. What is actually on exams or his in-class essay is a mystery and I often was blindsided.

analysis.name: Tobin Craig
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: The class is taught by different guest lectures which is made clear in the beginning of the course. I really found this class to be interesting and enjoyed it thoroughly. Dr. Craig is very knowledgeable and his lectures were amazing. The class has different guest lecturers and topics each class, all of which were interesting. But, the exams were very difficult as you're given little to no grading criteria and the answers they're looking for are very specific. Grading is tougher than a 100-level course should be.

Craig was honestly one of my favorite professors this semester. He truly knows his craft and lectures well. If you choose his class ensure you go to his office hours for participation. There's a lot of reading in this class however, participation in class discussions is highly encouraged but not forced. He is a hard grader however.

Professor Craig is a very good professor. He is quite anti-technology, so beware of that, but many of the PTCD faculty are. He is overall a great teacher though and makes himself very available. Not an easy professor, but if you pay attention in class and do most of the readings, you'll do just fine.

If you're a PTCD major this doesn't apply to you, as I am sure he is a great PTCD professor. Taking MC201 with him as a freshman was absolutely horrid. Very harsh grader. If you are someone who is not interested in political theory, and you were planning on taking him for any other type of class, don't.

analysis.name: Karenanna Creps
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: I actually took Karenanna for TE 432, Learning Through Movement, and she was incredible. I highly suggest her for this class.

She is super nice and easy to reach out to. I would send her my assignments to look over and she would always respond very quickly with helpful feedback. She lets you redo any assignment with a low grade even if it's from the beginning of the year. She makes learning fun and creative. Totally recommend her for Learning Through Drama.
Love her! Recommend 10/10 for the Learning through Drama class!! Easy to talk to:)

analysis.name: William Crank
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I appreciate that he used his own experiences in the business in lectures, as that gave applications and context to lectures. However, that's how he gave lectures. Almost purely through his own experiences. You have so few opportunities to earn a grade, so every little thing matters. This course caused so much stress. If you can, avoid his classes.

Yea so William Crank got cranky and made me stay after class to give me a lecture on being on time. I also was surprised by how much he bragged. He would  brag about things way off topic all time. If you tell him you know something he might argue you or brag he is better at it.

Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He does really care about the future of his students and constantly would bring up opportunities and opened himself up to help guide students which I thought was really nice. The exams are a little hard but if you show up to class you will understand whats going on. The group project was pretty easy too.

I am currently taking PR 305 with him this class is easily the worst class I have taken at msu He does not make any assignment clear every assignment he will not provide exact details of what he wants us to include. Most of the time he just talks about himself & prides himself that his exams r 15 pages single spaced & that they are not passable.

Crank is a piece of work. Easily one of the worst professors on campus, but is a God in his own mind. Never take this man, as he will make your semester 10x harder than it needs to be. (He is also the type of guy to read all these negative views on him, and conclude everyone but him is the problem.)

analysis.name: Sean Crosson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crosson is the greatest thing to ever walk into a biology classroom. He is super nice and very eager to help students understand the material. The class is flipped, which takes some getting used to, but he always does a recap at the beginning of class, which is very helpful. Also he had a little texas accent so he is fun to listen to.

Dr. Crosson is probably the best BS 161 professor you can find at MSU, however, he only teaches every 2 years so be mindful when you are scheduling for this class. Every other BS 161 professor needed to be switched out in the middle of the semester except for him because he was actually knowledgable on the topic unlike the others as I hear it.

Dr. Crosson is a thorough professor and is good at what he does. He is very knowledgable in the content and is super caring/understanding! The book is required, but it does not really help that much and the main content is in the lectures/ICAS. Extra credit opportunities are offered for exams 1-3(1 point each). I recommend him!

BS 161 was a very difficult and consuming class, but Dr. Crosson and his TAs/UALs were phenomenal. Without them I would have failed this class without a doubt, but they did an amazing job of helping every student who needed it and explaining the why behind the processes. Dr. Crosson is truly a great professor, and I wish I could have him again.

Hard class, but great professor. You get used to the stupid schedule, but it's a flipped classroom, so you teach yourself everything, then recap with questions and examples in class. Lot's of homework and studying. Iclicker questions also count for a grade. Crosson is great at answering questions in depth, so try and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Robert Cummiskey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy. I had a mental health crisis halfway through the semester and went from being there everyday to missing most classes. He was super understanding and had no problem accommodating me through that time. Also a super light grader as long as you put effort in. I would happily take this course again if I had to, great GPA boost.

I loved Dr. Bob! He made a gen-ed writing class very enjoyable. There are only 5 essays, or "projects" that you have to complete over the course of the semester, and as long as you stick to the rubric you will be fine. On top of being hilarious, he also gave me really good feedback that I could put towards my future essays.

Bob is a great and funny guy. The class he teaches is pretty easy. As long as you show effort, you'll get a good grade. The only problem is that he talks a lot. His lectures can go on a very long time because he goes on long tangents and repeats himself often. Other than that he's very helpful and nice. His lectures can drag but he's still great.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about you, Mr. Cummiskey is your guy. He is super considerate and is willing to work with you if you communicate. Great teacher, would definitely recommend for WRA 101.

Prof. Cummiskey is very casual and a great guy to interact with. If you show up to class and participate, he'll remember you and be more likely to help out when you need it. Class was very easy, mostly documentaries with writing projects throughout the semester. Very easy class to take for the IAH credit, plus it's a very fascinating subject.

analysis.name: Curtis VanDonkelaar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Curtis is an entertaining professor who cares a lot about his students, loves his job, and grades easily. That being said, he also assigns a myriad of homework at times, but he is very flexible with due dates. His lectures often have groupwork, and many assignments are peer review, so beware if that is not up your alley.

He is a really nice guy and if you participate a little he is super willing to help you and be accommodating. He does not put grades in which sucks but he gives you a lot of time for each project and gives really good feedback. Just show up and do the work and you'll be fine. He says attendance is mandatory but you can miss 2-3 times.

Doesn't put in grades until last minute BUT it's a fair and good amount of workload, if you miss one class you're fine. You get 4 absences through the semester. He's very very very caring and understanding and wants you to learn and understand course material. He is an amazing professor and very passionate of what he teaches.

He was an amazing professor, but my only complaint is that he did not grade any assignments until after finals, so I worried a bit about how he grades. All the assignments are very clear to complete and he allows you to turn in assignments late. Not a harsh grader, got a 4.0 in the class.

Really nice and caring guy. He just wants you to show up and participate. Do the work and you'll get a 4.0. Overall super easy class with an even better professor. Highly recommend taking this course with him.

analysis.name: Everardo Cuevas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He claimed that my paper was done by ai, which it wasn't and gave me a horrible grade. There was nothing I could do cause it was the end of the year. He is ALWAYS late to class and will cancel it 10 min before it starts when everyone is already in the classroom. Unprofessional and expects a lot when he doesn't hold himself to the same standards.

Dr. Eve was an amazing professor that taught a very well structured English class. He was very caring to all students and grades pretty leniently. Do your work when assigned and you should be able to easily get a 4.0.

Professor Cuevas is an excellent teacher. He's fun, helpful, and genuinely passionate about teaching — something that's increasingly rare these days. A professor who actively engages with students and truly wants them to learn already goes above and beyond. Show up to class, put effort into your projects/peer reviews and you'll 4.0 this course.

Professor Cuevas is truly one of the best professors I have had at MSU. He is so laid back and understanding. Communication is key in his class and despite any sense of intimidation you may have, there is no way to fail unless you are simply not even trying. Always always communicate with Cuevas and your results in this course will be great!

I really recommend Eve, he is a great guy along with an amazing teacher. Attendance is required for this class by the school, and the class is graded based on 5 projects/attendance. You should get a 4.0 if you show up and put in effort into the projects/online posts. The only thing that sucks is the grading scale used by the school - 94% is a 3.5

analysis.name: Katharine  Currie
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Currie made an easy class way too difficult. She explains things well but doesn't set you up for success. Her lectures miss a lot of important info and her exams are almost impossible to take. Her lab assignments also seem so useless and set you up for a low grade. If she wants students to do better she should redesign her slides and assignments.

She never adds any of the important points during lecture into her slides. If you want to succeed in this class, you have to heavily take notes which is almost impossible. Her exams are so bad and impossible to study for. She also does not set up assignments very well. If you miss one thing, you are not allowed to complete other requirements.

Professor Currie's lectures are long and have a lot of confusing info, I found it easier to not attend and study it at my own pace. However, she gives few extra credit points for attendance. The labs were frustrating for me as the pre quizzes were hard and you dont get alot of time. The lab TAs dont really help you for the lab reports either.

The material is interesting. The class would be so much better with a different professor though. Great person. Not great at explaining things. Some student have done really well. I am not one of those students. The material is confusing and she confuses me more with the way she explains things. Overall, this class sucks but you can do well in it.

analysis.name: Oscar Cuncic
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is the co-lecturer with prof Bauer. He teaches stuff really well in lectures. He will explain questions with great detail and I really enjoy attending his class. Sometimes he will even put corresponding hw questions on presentation slides. Turns out I believe this is a better way of teaching since we now truly understand how this question works.

His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Attendance is required and he uses iclicker to check the grades. The test study guides he makes are important. If you can do those, you can do the exam.  He has a generous extra credit policy.

Professor Cuncic is very passionate about physics. He is helpful and responsive to feedback. He is exactly what I would hope for from a physics professor at MSU. I am happy with how things turned out in this course and I would take any course with him teaching.
Attendance is mandatory. His lectures covered what would be on the exams, also the practice exams were similar to the exams. But the class is almost entirely based on exam grades.
Very passionate in his lectures. Participation matters a fair amount regarding iClicker. Practice exams are extremely similar to the real exams.

analysis.name: Allison Cupples
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: This class is not hard but you do need to make sure you go through the lectures and review before exams because the exams are not open note. Her lectures are kind of boring but make sure to pay attention bc it will be on the exams and homework. The final exam is not cumulative it just a regular exam.

Overall, a great class and professor. Everything you need to know she teaches you in lecture, the book is a nice addition but not necessary. The exams are a little challenging and require knowledge from lectures and homework, but overall, pretty fair. Attendance/participation not really required as she has recorded lectures on D2L. HWK once a week.

On exams be prepared to be tested on calculations as well as definitions and fill in the blank. If you go to lectures you should have no problem in this class. Cuppules is an amazing professor who prepares you for hw and exams extremely well with class lectures, I would recommend making flashcards for definitions, take notes

Nice lady! The notes she gives are clear and the homework is totally manageable and actually helps with the exams. The lectures could stand to be a little more interesting, but overall a good class, and an easy A.

analysis.name: Alison Cupples
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cupples is fantastic. All information on exams and homework is gone over in class. Lectures can be a little boring, but overall she is a good professor and prepares you well for exams. As long as you go to class this is an easy A.

One of the best professors I've had. She is extremely kind and her lectures are great. The homework follows the lecture examples and the tests are very similar to the homework. If you show up and pay attention, you'll be fine.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!!!! I missed class once, and you're allowed to miss three, and i will be lucky to 1.5 this class. It's so hard, she is TERRIBLE and extremely unhelpful. She expects you to memorize all the material and then decides to not test you on the "performance objectives" that she tells you to know. Avoid her at all costs!!!!

analysis.name: Cynthia Gabriel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: There's too much for just 350 characters, but I will say be prepared for your final to be a big group project. Super interesting!

She is extremely confusing. Everything is thrown onto the syllabus including due dates (which are changed verbally but not on the syllabus) so any time there is an assignment you have to dig through the entire syllabus. For a university requirement class the workload is a lot (if you actually do everything).  Conclusion: unorganized

unlike the other rater i loved our project because she gave us time in class to work on it. it was actually quite easy. and interesting. she gave us a lot of creative freedom with the project. and i thought the discussions were really interesting, but i didn't love listening to the rest of the students so much.

For a class with more than 200 people I can't believe how "small" she makes this class feel. I got to know other students. I love her lecture style. Some students want more "textbook"-style, but I prefer the way she has an organization structure to lecture but just talks without notes.

analysis.name: Cynthia Craig

wow, she is such a powerful force of nature...the best prof i have had yet!!!!!!

analysis.name: Sejuti Das Gupta

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Das Gupta; she makes sure you understand the content and even gives visual aids. Her midterm was open-note, and she even let us redo our first essay after she graded it and left comments. Das Gupta is the best teacher I have ever had here at MSU so far, and will probably sustain that role for the years coming. Overall, super caring and helpful

analysis.name: Don DeVeaux
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Professor DeVeaux has been one of the best professors I have ever had during my time at MSU. He cares so deeply for his students by structuring his course in a way that is both digestible and challenging. His lectures are so well prepared and very interesting. It truly reinforced my passion for Marketing and Market Research as a career.
